Dark_Blood_Fleet_Staging_Point.name: Dark Blood Fleet Staging Point
intro:
The Dark Blood Fleet Staging Point is an unrated cosmic signature site that can be scanned using Core Probes in Blood Raider infested regions of Null Sec space. It may also be received as an escalation from Blood Forsaken Hub and 
Blood Forlorn Hub anomalies. The site itself escallates twice, involving travel. If both escallations go in the same direction, you could end up in hostile space for part 3.

This can be run in a single Ishtar. The site appears to not aggro on Ishtar drones, so reset the aggro if that happens. The most critical part of running this is to deal with the neut batteries. Primary them but run away while you do because incoming damage will be heavy and you won't have cap. Fits with 100mn ABs and especially drone navigation modules, to get to the neut batteries faster may be best. Note that non-capital dark blood modules vary widely in price and so the site may not be worth running. It takes a long time. I destroyed all the batteries, but I recommend only destroying the neut batteries.

pockets.title: 2nd Pocket
pockets.prose: Killing the Corpus Pope will proceed the site to stage 2

notes.title: Warp-in
notes.text: No hostiles on warpin.

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.text: This site can escalate, and I believe it may be guaranteed to do so, to Dark Blood Fleet Staging Point 2.

messages:
Intelligence indicates this site is a fleet staging area for the Blood Raider Covenant. Resources and ships travel to this location from a remote base, coming here to re-arm and refuel. Elimination of forces at the staging area should reveal the location of the remote base.

DED Threat Assessment: 9 of 10

Scans show that the nearby supply cache has been used to store goods stolen from another system. The Blood Raiders likely have a larger contingent there, and coordinates have been uploaded to the Expedition panel in your NeoCom Journal.

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text: This expedition is in nullsec, with all four parts in Sansha infested nullsec. A high DPS ship is recommended to take out Naberius Marquis in the final location.

messages: Going through the logs from one of the command ships you blasted, you come across a recent memo containing a draft for a plan where forces from this Military Complex and another similar to this one were to gang up and raid a space trucker station somewhere in the region. Where this space trucker station is, is not included in the logs, but the location of the rally point is there. It is supposed to be by a small asteroid belt, not too far away.
Sansha Minion Scout: Send me the secret password NOW. I'm warning you ...
From the wreckage of this ship, you get info on where it is from, it is another Sansha station. Well, more an outpost than a station perhaps, but it is a pure military outfit, not a regular colony.
You scan the wreck for further info, examine the location and listen for a while on all channels ... but nothing. It seems you have lost the trail of this raiding party.
Again you let your scanners comb the remains of the station and the ships, looking for clues on this alleged raid, but alas .. nothing, not a word anywhere.

Again you let your scanners comb the remains of the station and the ships, looking for clues on this alleged raid, and before long you are holding a log listing the second rally spot and as far as you can see, the raiding parties have already departed from here and two other stations and are supposed to convene within the hour. If one of the raiding parties was supposed to come from the Sansha station you destroyed originally, you have already managed to diminish their forces somewhat.

A fixed guidance beacon sitting here all alone .. you examine the thing and discover its guidance system points to a place not too far away. Perhaps that is the space trucker station? In any case, that is the only clue you have to follow, if the pirates have ever been here, they have gone already.
A peaceful station, where transport ships get refitted and refueled. Almost too peaceful ...
Space Trucker Convoy: To all nearby ships. I think we might have trouble. Let's go back through the gate before something happens!

Sansha Raider: Clear out the guards first!
Sansha Raiders have appeared!

More Sansha have appeared.
Sansha Raider: I will loot these guys, you get the hangars!

A Sansha Relay Scout has warped in from a nearby area. More Sansha have appeared.
Sansha Raider: Looks like there might be trouble, boys. Get ready for a fight!

The True Sansha leader, Naberius Marquis, has arrived.
Naberius Marquis: Let's see what we have here. A pitiful little space trucker encampment protected by a few inbred mercenaries. Looks like we'll have some fun tonight, minions.
Space Trucker mercenaries have come through the gate to defend it!
The trail appears to run cold at this point.

Desolate_Site.name: Desolate Site
intro:
Desolate Site is an Unrated Complex found in high sec and low sec via exploration.

You must be flying a T3 cruiser or smaller to enter the acceleration gate.

pockets.title: Walkthrough
pockets.prose:
Initially there are only two groups on grid. Third group consisting of a frigate and a destroyer appears in few seconds. You can ignore the groups that have destroyers or drones. Destroying the group with frigates only will trigger additional waves.

The first and second spawns appear by the Warning Sign structure.

Finishing first spawn can trigger escalation.

rows.name: Sentient Devilfish Alvi
rows.cargo: Drops Drone material, has a chance to drop the Rogue drone 46-X chip

rewards.title: Loot
rewards.text:
* Salvage: 814K-1.42M
* Loot: (sentient drone) Drone Capillary Fluids + Drone Synaptic Relay Wiring (~5m). Possible Rogue Drone 46-X Nexus Chip (~50m). Sentient Modules (~100m) (very rare).
* Bounties: about 50k (defenders) and 80k (reinforcement)

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.text: Destroying the first spawn group or sentient drone can escalate the site to Mare Sargassum.

messages: Rogue Drones are unpredictable, pilots are advised to tread with care.

At first it seems strange the drones have picked this barren and resource deficient place to build a new hive. But then again, while you were blowing up the place, you noticed a few vessels that might have been used as transports, indicating the drones were pulling in the materials they needed from someplace else. As to compliment you on your reasoning, your communication systems start indicating several different incoming transmissions in drone beeps and clicks and after a while you manage to coerce your instruments into pointing out an approximate spatial origin of the message.

Gate Sentries deal heavy damage so you should have good overall resists (for EM/Thermal) and good buffer or active tank with repair capabilities. It is suggested to tank the incoming damage and destroy the webbing towers while moving away from the sentries which are hard to destroy. With sufficient distance (approx. 50km) sentries stop dealing damage so you can concentrate on pirate ships. Structure itself drop common loot and very hard to destroy so you can also skip destroying it and focus on hacking cans.

Dirty_Site.name: Dirty Site
intro:
Dirty Site is an Unrated Complex found in lowsec via exploration.

The site is behind an acceleration gate. Warping to the site lands you at 0 on the gate.

pockets.title: Room 1
pockets.prose: Acceleration gate is 25 km from warp-in.

pockets.title: Room 2
pockets.prose: Additional spawns are mostly (only?) triggered by killing frigates. Shoot triggers with caution; it is very easy to trigger multiple waves at once and the large amount of elite cruisers and battlecruisers can do serious damage.

rows.name: Harvester/Infectious Drone
rows.trigger: killing all Infectious drones triggers commander wave. killing Harvester drones triggers other spawns

rows.name: Sentient Violator Alvum
rows.cargo: Drone components, possible 43-X Nexus chip or Sentient faction modules

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.text: Can escalate to Loose Ends.

messages: From one of the drone ship databases your sensors burst through as you tore this hive-in-the-making apart, you gain information on something that seems to be small satellite ops. The info is largely a listing of varied equipment, dates of when it arrived here, its quality and lastly; coordinates to a couple of these places.

Domination_Surveillance_Squad.name: Domination Surveillance Squad
intro: Domination Surveillance Squad is an Expedition that can escalate from Provisional Angel Outpost.

pockets.title: First Location
pockets.prose: Kill Domination cruiser, loot wreck, possibly get escalation. Otherwise take the Newly Constructed Acceleration Gate.

rows.name: Domination Predator/Centurion/...
rows.cargo: Faction ammo/tags; Possible Domination faction modules or implants

pockets.title: First Pocket
pockets.prose: There are two groups of NPCs present at warp-in. One will warp off. Destroy the Angel Security Station to get escalation.

rows.name: Domination Centurion/Phalanx
rows.cargo: Faction ammo/tags; Possible Domination faction modules or implants

pockets.title: First Pocket
pockets.prose:
Like the first location, you land 60 km away from an Angel Security Station structure. Destroying this structure may trigger escalation.
 Rats do not aggro until you approach or attack. There are two groups, one of which will warp away after a few seconds.

pockets.title: Third Location
pockets.prose: Take acceleration gate if Domination cruiser does not spawn or trigger escalation.

rows.name: Domination Liquidator/Marauder
rows.cargo: Faction ammo/tags. Possible Domination modules or a rare implant

pockets.title: First Pocket
pockets.prose: Simple warp-in can trigger escalation. Unlike the first two locations, you have auto-aggro the moment you land in the pocket.

pockets.title: Fourth Location
pockets.prose:
Ungated pocket, with debris, rocks, and an Elysian structure. No rats are initially present at warp-in.

Attacking the Elysian structure also triggers multiple smartbomb waves.
Note that warping off for too long may 'reset' the smartbomb trigger, causing another set of waves when your return.

Nikmar Eitan has a strong passive shield tank compared to the other NPCs, and has a 2.5 million ISK bounty on him.

rows.name: Nikmar Eitan
rows.cargo: Gistum C-Type cruiser modules, possible Domination faction modules or a rare Cynabal BPC

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text: The first three locations are usually in low security space and the last in null security space, but this can vary. For locations #1-3, take the Newly Constructed Acceleration Gate into the first pocket if no escalation is given from destroying the commander or if the commander ship does not spawn. Gistum Breaker/Defeater cruisers rarely web.

rewards.title: Loot
rewards.text: The Domination commanders drop faction ammo and tags, and may also contain Domination cruiser modules. Nikmar Eitan may drop Gistum C-Type cruiser modules or a rare Cynabal BPC.

messages: It seemed for a while you would manage to get all of the Angels, but evidently one ship from the Domination Angels has slipped away. Luckily your scanners seem to have gathered enough information to give you its approximate destination.

The station databanks contain information on the local Domination Angel security network and among it; a location of yet another station similar to this one. That is your best clue as to where the ships that fled as you entered have gone.
To your dismay, the main computers of this station took a direct hit during your assault and any information that might have been there is gone up in smoke.

To your dismay, the main computers of this station took a direct hit during your assault and any information that might have been there is gone up in smoke.However, your instruments ran through the data from the fleeing ships and have come up with this location as a suggestion to where they might have warped.
Hodura Amaba: What goes on here? Who dares disturb us?

It looks like the most interesting of these Domination ships got away during the fight. Luckily for you though, one of its communication devices seems to be malfunctioning and is for no apparent reason sending out a constant stream of gurgling sounds. Your instruments have no problems tracing where it is coming from. It is an extremely irritating sound. Aggravating too. The gurgling of doom.
The pirate station has activated a smartbomb, damaging all hostile ships within its range!

The pirate station has called on reinforcements from a nearby deadspace pocket.
More pirate reinforcements have arrived.
Nikmar Eitan: Noooo! You've just ruined years of research. I can't believe it. You will PAY for that, mongrel!

For a while there, you almost wished you had brought more friends with you and you are relieved you managed to blow the station before more could scramble against you. You are also relieved you managed to kill off that blasted gurgle sound. Permanently.

Dread_Guristas_Fleet_Staging_Point.name: Dread Guristas Fleet Staging Point
intro: Dread Guristas Fleet Staging Point is an Unrated Complex found by scanning in Null Security systems with Guristas presence. It can also be received as an escalation from a Guristas Forsaken Hub or Guristas Hidden Rally Point.

pockets.title: First pocket
pockets.prose: The first pocket is fairly straightforward and easy. Destroy initial spawn, blow up the trigger last, destroy wave 2, take the gate.

blocks.title: Initial defenders (45-55 km from acceleration gate)

pockets.title: Second pocket
pockets.prose:
Get ready to blow up the energy neutralizing sentries when you warp in; they add a lot of difficulty to the room.

The site does not contain any noteworthy loot.

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text:
This site is fairly hard due to large number of ships and neuting towers. It can be done in a group of T2, T3 or Faction cruisers or a few battleships.

Warping to the site lands you at 0 on an acceleration gate.

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.text: The site has an almost 100% chance to escalate to Dread Guristas Fleet Staging Point 2.

messages:
The massive amounts of signatures you are getting on your short range scan can only indicate one thing, a full combat fleet in station around the deadspace pocket. The Guristas Pirates would seem to be planning a large scale military operation in the area and you should expect nothing but the heaviest resistance should you try to oppose them here.
DED Threat Assessment: Extreme (9 of 10)
The last Guristas Pirate Battleship sends out a distress signal before it goes down. Luckily your com systems have managed to decrypt the message and follow it to it's final destination.

Dread_Guristas_Fleet_Staging_Point_2.name: Dread Guristas Fleet Staging Point 2
Dread_Guristas_Fleet_Staging_Point_2.signature: Escalates from Dread Guristas Fleet Staging Point
intro: Dread Guristas Fleet Staging Point 2 is an Expedition that can escalate from Dread Guristas Fleet Staging Point.

pockets.title: Warp-in
pockets.prose:
You land on a beacon.

Wave 2 triggers when the penultimate battleship in initial spawn is attacked.

Wave 3 triggers when the last battleship in initial spawn is attacked.

The Guristas Scout Commander does not have significant tank, like a regular Overseer Cruiser. Its wreck may produce T2 salvage materials, though.

Destroying the commander (and possibly, failing that, all ships) will trigger an escalation to Dread Guristas Fleet Staging Point 3. To blitz, then, kill battleships until the elite frigates spawn, then kill the Overseer cruiser.

The acceleration gate to the first pocket does not have to be used; the first pocket is optional, and only worth doing for extra bounties/salvage.

rows.name: Guristas Scout Commander
rows.cargo: May contain 12th Tier Overseer's Personal Effects or Dread Guristas faction modules

rows.name: Acceleration Gate
rows.note: Locked until all ships are destroyed

pockets.title: First Pocket
pockets.prose:
Only go in here if you want bounties/salvage. No escalation is triggered here.

Highly recommend destroying the stasis tower and neuting sentry first; they add a lot of difficulty to this room.

rows.name: Guristas Energy Neutralizer Sentry III
rows.note: Has a strong passive tank and neuts 40 GJ/s

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text: The site is considerably harder than the unrated complex due to heavy neuting and webbing, as well as high DPS. Again, a fleet of T2, T3 or Faction Cruisers or a small group of Battleships is recommended for this site.

messages: The last Guristas Battleship sends out a distress signal before it goes down. Luckily your com systems have managed to decrypt the message and follow it to it's final destination.

You observe the remnants of a small outpost, probably used by smugglers or perhaps it was a small mining colony. All that remains now are dust and echoes.

You have located the ruins of an old station. The structure, once-magnificent, is now only a barren, airless derelict, its halls home to nothing but mechanical malevolence.

Drone_Horde.name: Drone Horde
intro:
Drone Horde is an unrated combat site belonging to the Rogue Drones faction. It can be found via exploration as a cosmic anomaly in null-security systems across New Eden. As an ungated complex, the limitations as to which ships can complete this site are tied to the security rating of the system where the anomaly spawns (T2 Battleships for high-security systems, and up to Titans in low-security and null-security systems). 

This site comes in two forms: One which cointains a turret ring and a cloud gas centering a structure, and other that has 4 bunkers in the middle and many scattered in the corners of a square pattern.

pockets.title: Walkthrough (4-Bunker Variant)
pockets.prose:
This site contains four bunkers at 30km from landing and four other separated in a square pattern centering the bunker cluster. The initial wave spawns scattered at the "corners" of that square, all next waves spawn near the central bunker cluster. The site shows some major inconsistencies regarding the order and timing of wave spawning, resulting in some iterations spawning more than one wave at once, and in others skipping one entirely. There is incoming EM in this site (Alvus Queen, Exterminator Alvatis)

Removing battleships from the initial wave will trigger two additional waves before the complete removal of the initial wave.

One of those two waves will consist of frigates and some bigger ships, the other of cruisers and bigger ships.

After the complete removal of the initial spawn and the two additional waves, the site will sequentially spawn these five additional waves (in a random order):

With the last wave, there is a chance of a rare spawn

blocks.title: 1x Destroyer & Battleship wave; Consistently the last wave

rows.name: Strain Splinter / Render / Decimator / Infester Alvi
Marauder Alvus / Matriarch Alvus / Alvus Queen
Strain Devastator / Violator Alvum / Viral Infector

notes.title: Walkthrough (Gas Ring Variant)
notes.text: Features a structure 30km app. from landing, 8x Lookout Tokers and a Battlecruiser as the initial spawn. Waves are spawned on different points of an horizontal ring with a 20km radius centering the middle structure. Each of these waves spawns a little deployable (not lootable) that diminishes incoming damage. This combat site has a chance to spawn a Sentient Commander Rogue Drone, which drops drone components and may drop faction drone modules and items.

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.text: Both sites may escalate to Outgrowth Rogue Drone Hive (10/10)

Drone Infested Mine

Strain Disintegrator Alvum / Strain Bomber Alvum

messages: In Local (after flying around the ruined gallente station)
Your sensors are picking up a signal...

Having waited for this devious Blood Raider for a while, you are starting to think he is not going to show up at all. You kind of feel used... but on the other hand, you got to rob some more Blood Raiders.

Finally your communication instruments come alive as this devious Blood Raider who hired you starts talking on the private channel. Even though the place was empty, he commends you on a job well done and gives you directions to the next assassination target.
This time your employer is right on time with the coordinates to the last location. He sounds somewhat stressed, but before you can reply he is gone.

This time your employer does not let you wait, with a more hissy voice than before he thanks you for services rendered and congratulates you on being scammed for a good cause. And with that he is off the air, permanently this time. It is true that having some reward for your efforts would be nice, but then again, you got to kill some Blood Raiders who would otherwise still be alive.

After blowing up his third rival, you have probably come closer than you ever will to hear how a sadistic head honcho with the Blood Raider Covenant sounds when he is ecstatically pleased. He gives you one last location, tells you to come meet him there and take with you everything you looted from the three raids. It is payday.
Upon death of Dark Corpus Preacher...
You have always been a bit ambivalent to having a day job, mostly due to several of your previous employers being bastards. This one however was ok, if only you could have more like him.

Video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EWKnWNtkd2s Ishtar + Buzzard]

pockets.title: Walkthrough
pockets.prose:
The pocket is ungated. There is quite a bit of optional combat. If you want to avoid combat with the NPCs, warp at a distance to the site and draw the NPCs away from the hacking containers, then warp at 0 to the containers and hack while they try to slowboat back to the containers. 

Otherwise make a bouncing bookmark 150-200 km away from the NPCs and containers, warp into the site (you should fit for some tank) and hack the containers while ignoring the NPCs. The containers can be opened even if the NPCs nearby are left alive. Note that if you draw the NPCs too far away (~200 km) they will teleport back to their starting positions.

The NPCs have special names but are just renamed Angel deadspace rats so they don't drop anything extraordinary.

messages:
Business arrangements between the Angel Cartel and the Serpentis corporation have never been more lucrative, well organized or complimentary. With each new push into booster research both parties edge closer to atteining mutual aims. Covering thier partner's weaknesses and suplementing thier strengths.

When the leadership of the Cartel, the Domination Angels, received word that Serpentis CEO Salvador Sarpati was mobilizing forces toward low-sec, not only did they rally Guardian Angel forces to protect Serpentis assets, they also began to devise a new form of protection unlike any they had ever provided before. If the Serpentis Corporation's own drug bases were ever to fail, the X-Instinct and Sooth Sayer production facilities managed by the Guardian Elohim would help ensure that not everything had been lost. DED are said to be aware of the situation and yet powerless to stop what is fast becoming the most fearsome pirate cooperative ever formed.

Emerging_Conduit.name: Emerging Conduit
intro: The Emerging Conduit combat site appeared as an anomaly in all areas of high security space regardless of the presence of Triglavian Invasions between October 2019 and May 2020.

pockets.title: Contents
pockets.prose:
The site consists of single ungated normal space pocket. Three waves of increasing difficulty will spawn with next wave appearing after previous wave has been killed. The rats in the site will use various types of EWAR: Energy neutralizing, tracking disruptors, guidance disruptors, webs and target painters. The site does not have warp disrupting or warp scrambling enemies.

Frigates are the most common enemy type in the site. Each wave will usually contain one or two destroyers with rest of the ships being frigates.

Wave 1: 3-6 Frigates/destroyers (Kikimora/Damavik).

Wave 2: 4-7 Frigates/destroyers (Kikimora/Damavik) and a chance of a named Kikimora (Zorya's Kikimora).

Wave 3: 9 Frigates/destroyers (Kikimora/Damavik) and a named Vedmak (Zorya's Vedmak).

blocks.title: Wave 1(EWAR not confirmed, can be random)
Wave 2(EWAR not confirmed, can be random)

rows.trigger: Triggers wave 3 if left as last ship

blocks.title: Wave 3(EWAR not confirmed, can be random)

rows.cargo: Possible faction modules, Triglavian materials

notes.title: History
notes.text:
Emerging Conduits were introduced in October 2019, during Chapter 1 of the Triglavian Invasion. The site uses an identical layout to Minor Conduits, with significantly weaker waves, and no scrams. Initially on a 1 minute respawn timer, people claimed that they could earn as much as 500M ISK/hr across three characters using smartbomb Praxii. The respawn time was later nerfed to 10 minutes in January 2020, lowering its farmability.

This iteration of conduits were removed in May 2020, alongside the beginning of chapter 3 of the invasion. New versions of Emerging Conduits have replaced them, now exclusive to Invasion space.

Emerging Conduits no longer exist.

notes.title: Tactics
notes.text:
The rats will spawn on top of the rift at the center of the site. This is ~70 km from the warpin. The frigates and destroyers will orbit at ~6 km range making webs and grapplers highly effective once they are in range. 

Frigates have a speed of ~3 km/s and a range of ~20 km. Destroyers have a speed of ~1.5 km/s and a range of ~30 km. Zorya's Vedmak has a speed of 2.3 km/s and a range of 35 km. EWAR weapons have longer ranges. Incoming damage from the waves spike up to 1k to 1.5k per second during the final wave (earlier waves are easier/deal less damage). 

Kiting them is technically possible, but the fits required to maintain the speed and distance leave very little room for dps. 

The typical tactic is to stay where you warped in and let them come to you, which gives you time to target them and be ready for the next wave, or, as some are selecting the closest Talassonite asteroid and warping 70km from it allowing you to land directly on to the rift that they spawn from.

The site can be completed solo with a heavily tanked passive shield tank battleship - Rattlesnake is the most obvious choice. Other known (successful) options include Leshak, Dominix, Dominix Navy Issue, Drekavac, Praxis and Vindicator. It can also be done with Dual Shield Rep Dominix or Praxis, but they require high drone skills for the proper dps and would require two or more pilots. 

The rats deal quite high damage but they also switch aggro quite often. This makes it possible to complete the site in a group of ships that can tank the incoming damage in bursts but not sustain the tank.

The named rats (Zorya's Vedmak/Kikimora) will warp off if not killed early and is not required to be killed to trigger the next wave. The Zorya's Kikimora will randomly spawn only in the second wave, and if left as the last ship in that second wave, it will trigger the third wave. It is recommended to kill them early in their respective wave to maximize loot and to avoid spawning the next wave early or having them warp off. 

Triglavian damage from their regular weapons is Thermal/Explosive and their defense weakness is also Thermal/Explosive. In addition, some Triglavians (the Liminal, the (non-prefix)Raznaborg and Zorya's variants) will also fire 'Majorana' missiles that deal heavy EM/Kinetic damage(270 for Raznaborg Damaviks). Therefore, an omni tank is highly recommended.

rewards.title: Rewards
rewards.text:
Completing the site will pay 4.5 million isk and 300 DED LP to each pilot present on site. If more than three pilots are on site the payout will be reduced.

The different payouts are as follows. No matter how many pilots are in the conduit after three pilots, the combined max payout is 13.5 million isk. 

1 to 3 Players - 4.5 Million isk each
* 1 Player - 4.5 Million isk Total
* 2 Players - 9 Million isk Total
* 3 Players - 13.5 Million isk Total

4 Players - 3.375 Million isk each
* 13.5 Million isk Total

5 Player - 2.7 Million isk each
* 13.5 Million isk Total

The Triglavian wrecks will often contain stacks of Triglavian Survey Databases and rarely abyssal filaments or mutaplasmids. Loot from the wrecks can vary from 150,000 isk to upwards of 50 million isk. 

The Triglavian Survey Databases can be either sold in a station, typically in trade hubs, to buy orders, or you can go to any Concord Station and sell them to Concord for 100,000 isk before in game taxes. 

Salvage from the Triglavian wrecks will drop materials used for T2 Triglavian ships.

Festering_Ruins.name: Festering Ruins
intro:
Festering Ruins is a combat relic site found in the [https://evemaps.dotlan.net/map/Fountain Fountain] nullsec region. Up to T2 Battleships can enter this site. This site appears to Probes as a combat site. 

The site is very rare and hard, and should only be attempted by skilled players. Rogue Drone, Serpentis, Angel Cartel and Guristas rats are present in this site. Omni tanks are highly recommended, especially against Kinetic and Thermal damage.

Compared to other combat relic sites, this is noticeably harder due to higher DPS, especially in the fourth and last pocket.

pockets.prose:
Expect high incoming damage in this room; recommend destroying the Stasis Towers first if you cannot tank the damage.

The "Gate to Portal" will lead to second pocket while the "Gate to Hall" leads to third pocket. Both are locked until all ships are destroyed.

messages: Pirate Grave Robber: The ancient ruins in here are taken buddy. Leave now and maybe we'll let you go in one piece.

DED deep space scouts briefly explored this strange site and left behind a rather cryptic note. As far as you can tell some ancient ruins lie within, but who built them or what treasures might lie buried there are anyone's guess.

Charred remains and debris litter the area. A confrontation between the pirate scavengers and rogue drones must have taken place some time in the past, as the empty drone bunkers and ruined pirate ship carcasses would indicate.

As you come out of acceleration you notice the resemblance of a space rift in the distance.
Core Relay Commander: They've found the portal! Destroy them before they escape !!
As the Relay Commander is attacked, he calls for backup! More hostile ships are incoming!
As the Relay Commander is attacked, he calls for backup! More hostile ships are incoming!

A large force of drones has taken up residence in this area. They obviously benefit greatly from salvaging the remnants of the former inhabitants, which still litters this patch of space. A drone presence this large could not be formed without an abundance of raw materials.

There are two Pulse Drones on grid and when they are attacked, they begin sending out waves of energy, gas and materials, hitting anything in its path. All ships anbd drones in the blast radius take damage!
Drones have been deployed from the Drone Bunkers in response to the attack on the sentry guns!
As the Pulse Drone is attacked, it starts sending out waves of energy, gas and materials, hitting anything in its path. All ships in the blast radius take damage!

The source of the drone infestation seems to lie in this deadspace pocket, located inside a fiery nebula. The extreme and hostile environment, accompanied by a very heavy drone presence, seems to have kept most of the looters away, as two fully intact ancient ruins would indicate.

messages: Without you noticing, a small group of the Blood ships slipped away at the beginning of the fight. Luckily your radar systems have picked up a trace leading to this location.
You have destroyed the pirate threat. Your sensors have recovered co-ordinates from one of the frigate wreckages.
You have destroyed the pirate threat. No further threat is detected.

As expected, the Blood tried to stop you. The fierceness of the ambush was great, even for Blood fighters and you wonder why they didn't just try to escape into the vastness of space.

Perhaps they are hiding something? After your systems have analyzed transmissions between the Blood ships during the fight, they come up with a location.

As weird as it was finding this shiny rock here in the middle of nowhere, it is a bit more understandable now, knowing it was only a sadistic trap laid out by the Blood.

Luckily you were well prepared and handled the threat with ease. One of the destroyed ships even revealed co-ordinates to a large Blood Raider base.

Even though you are not too well versed in the twisted ways of the Blood Raiders, you think it is a bit strange to find one of their cathedrals floating out here, completely in the middle of nowhere. But whatever its purpose was, it is irrelevant now; it isn't here anymore.

The final wave is the overseer wave. It spawns when the Blood Raider Military Outpost is at 55% structure.

notes.text: This expedition is a very hard one, and may require several people in strong ships (T3C, well-tanked Battleship or Marauder is advised). The first and second locations can be done solo, but the last two locations have very high incoming DPS that can overwhelm a ship running solo.

messages: As the dust settles from the battle, you receive a transmission from someone claiming to be a local vigilante who congratulates you on a job well done. Your computers run a check on his ship ID's and other info they can gather on him in such a short period of time, but come up with nothing. He appears to represent neither a pirate faction nor one of the empires. This person continues to welcome you to the area and offers to point you to some other Blood bases he knows about and have been a menace for the local population. If you want to come and meet him, he will lead the way.

Cura Gigno: Good to see you decided to come. I can not promise you any payment if you take on these Blood Raider bases, but you will earn fame among the locals and the fortune the Bloods leave behind. I'm going to send a couple of my spy drones to see if the Blood Raiders are still where they were yesterday.
The radio crackles with the vigilante's excited whispering. "They're still here! Come quick and we'll show them a whole new definition of pain!"
Control Tower Operator: More intruders! Maybe they're connected with the spy drones we just destroyed. I bet CONCORD sent them! Take care of 'em boys!
The Missile Battery was booby-trapped! As it explodes, it sends out a blast-wave triggered by a built-in smartbomb. All hostile ships caught in the blast take damage.
Cura Gigno: We sure showed them! I'm actually starting to think I'll become a fighter some day. Will you teach me? Maybe after we're done ...

"We sure did show them! You sure are better than no one to have around when the missiles are flying! But there is no time to float here fabulating, we must press on, another division of this same group is close by! I will pop over and scout, check if they are there still! " All these exclamation marks make you dizzy. It may well be that this guy is not much of a fighter, but he is no coward and you wonder if it is not hard to do scouting missions on an industrial ... Around 30 seconds later you receive a transmission "OMG the bastards have scrambled me !! I am getting killed here! Help! Help! I am at moon six, where is everyone, come .. "and then the transmission stops. You turn off the radio, there are too many "moon 6" around for you to go looking, and besides...

"We sure did show them! You sure are better than no one to have around when the missiles are flying! But there is no time to float here fabulating, we must press on, another division of this same group is close by! "

As you enter, you see your friend several hundred kilometers off target, complaining about something being rotten in the hydraulic system. With the Blood Raiders on the other hand, it seems like all systems are go.

Cura Gigno: I hope you will manage without me, but I am going to check the next and last target. It's one of the Blood's holy places, some Fountain of Youth thing, quite a splash! We don't want them to get away. I will hold them busy till you arrive!
The Defense Sentinel calls for backup from a nearby patrol!

"I will hold them busy till you arrive!" Yeah, right. The only way he is going to slow them down is to stun them with a steady flow of exclamation marks. The Dark Bloods are no joke. This innermost circle of the Blood Raiders is legendary for its brutality and the unparalleled skill of its pilots.
Your radio crackles to life again when this chatty would-be vigilante sends a message to his newfound friend: "Yes, they are here, and it seems the element of surprise is on our side! I suggest that you open with a full frontal assault so I can charge from the side, flank them, and then we can crush them between us! I will need to stay off the air for now, though: I am launching a covert ops through stealth tactics in order to get into position! Good luck !! "
Come to think of it, this guy might be a 12-year-old who has stolen his mom's ship. But there is nothing to wait for; there are the coordinates, and the enemy is waiting.

You see a spatial rift in the distance: This is probably what the Blood Raiders have called the "Fountain Of Youth." Perhaps it was usable at some point in the past, but your computer indicates it is currently so unstable that attempting to use it would mean certain death. You refrain from any thoughts of using it, for now.

Cura Gigno: Let me know if you need a hand! 
Cura Gigno: "Cura Gigno takes on the Blood Raiders." Yeah, I think I'll call my biography something like that. You can be my sidekick, maybe ... the silent warrior by my side. Maybe they'll even give me a medal! 
Cura Gigno: I'm impressed. You seem almost as good as I'd be flying that ship of yours ... 
Cura Gigno: I got your back! Keep it up! 
Cura Gigno: Wait! I'm still reloading !!
As the Military Outpost is attacked, a horde of defenders undock to defend it!

High Ritualist Padio Atour: So we meet at last. You are most likely the one that has been disrupting our operations recently. I must say, I'm impressed with your ability to crush my subordinates. But taking on me is an entirely different matter. 
Since you've done so well for yourself, I'll give you the comforting knowledge that your body will be sent to your family in one piece. And if you have any close relatives that show promise in the space-combat business, I'll make sure to offer them a place at my side.

This was a hard fight and even though your friend didn't fire many shots, he did his best to call them. Gutsy little fellow. You would think that by now he should have used half of all superlatives in the English language to describe your victory, but surprisingly enough he is dead silent there where he is orbiting the remains of this holy place. Closer inspection reveals that he has taken a direct hit and even though his ship looks intact, all the airlocks have been blasted out and either he must have died from the explosion, or he is lying there frozen from the exposure. It is kind of sad ... not that you will miss him personally, but you can be darn sure that if he had lived to run around and tell the story, you would have been a legendary hero 24 hours from now.

Not accurately enough though, as they warp out as soon as you enter space. Luckily your instruments manage to come up with a best approximation for their next destination.

During the fighting, the final ship managed to escape. Fortunately, your sensors picked up a distress signal from it and calculated a probable destination.
Obviously the distress signal made it through to the intended recipients, this was quite a reception. In any case, there are a bit less drug runners in space after this encounter...

messages: Going through the logs from one of the command ships you blasted, you come across a recent memo containing a draft for a plan where forces from this Military Complex and another similar to this one were to gang up and raid a space trucker station somewhere in the region. Where this space trucker station is, is not included in the logs, but the location of the rally point is there. It is supposed to be by a small asteroid belt, not too far away.
Killing Dark Blood Cardinal activates another escalation
From the wreckage of this ship, you get info on where it is from, it is another Blood station. Well, more an outpost than a station perhaps, but it is a pure military outfit, not a regular colony.
Again you let your scanners comb the remains of the station and the ships, looking for clues on this alleged raid, but alas ... nothing, not a word anywhere.

Again you let your scanners comb the remains of the station and the ships, looking for clues on this alleged raid, and before long you are holding a log listing the second rally spot and as far as you can see, the raiding parties have already departed from here and two other stations and are supposed to convene within the hour. messages: It seemed for a while you would manage to get all of the pirates, but evidently one of the guard ships from the Guardian Angels has slipped away. Luckily your scanners seem to have gathered enough information to give you its approximate destination.

The station databanks contain information on the local Guardian Angel security network and among it; a location of yet another station similar to this one. That is your best clue as to where the ships that fled as you entered have gone.

To your dismay, the main computers of this station took a direct hit during your assault and any information that might have been there is gone up in smoke. However, your instruments ran through the data from the fleeing ships and have come up with this location as a suggestion to where they might have warped.

It looks like a Serpentis executive vessel the angels were escorting got away during the fight. Luckily for you though, one of its communication devices seems to be malfunctioning and is for no apparent reason sending out a constant stream of sentimental and dreamy meditation muzak. Your instruments have no problems tracing where it is coming from. This wailing is extremely irritating. Aggravating in fact. The muzak of doom.
Upon structure death (in local chat channel)
Marin Matola: Noooo! You've just ruined years of research. I can't believe it. You will PAY for that, mongrel!
Expeditions - Guardian Angels Surveillance Squad (expedition end)

For a while there, you almost wished you had brought more friends with you and you are relieved you managed to blow the station before more could scramble against you. You are also relieved you managed to kill off that blasted gurgle sound. Permanently.

messages: Heuristic analysis of this location indicates that destroying the Guristas Experimental Control Tower would greatly improve your odds of uncovering further illicit activity.

Guristas are the ones of the pirate factions who one usually thinks about as common thugs and loosely organized at best, but as far as you could see, this here was actually an advanced weapon lab run by these "common thugs", something is not right and you let your scanners go to work on the stations remains. While studying the ruined structure and ships, you get hold of some logs containing communication records which lead you to believe that this here operation was contracted and financed by an outside agent, or at least someone who didn’t identify himself as a part of the Guristas. In these records there are lists of orders and deliveries, everything going through a place called Zelig’s patch. That name rings a bell... well, you don’t know it personally, but your computers quickly connect this name with an entry in the regional trade registry, this is a trader in high tech lubricants and he even has an address...

notes.title: Mining
notes.text:
Unfortunately, the acceleration gate is limited to frigate or destroyer-sized ships, so only mining frigates or expedition frigates can enter the site to mine. 

The site will stay loaded provided the Guristas Control Center is not destroyed. If it is destroyed, staying inside the site will keep it loaded. You can use an alt for this purpose. You may also briefly leave the site to drop off ore, but if the site is too far away from your drop-off point, the site may despawn if nobody is inside. It is best to leave someone in the site if possible just in case. Moving too far toward the outside on grid can also cause the site to despawn. If you want to further restrict who can come into the site, purposefully destroying the Guristas Control Center will remove the site signature and restrict its access to bookmarks and combat probes.

It is recommended to use an Endurance to mine the site, as its larger mining hold will minimize drop-offs to unload your cargo. It also lets you use light scout drones to defeat all rats in each pocket and reinforcements that include ECM rats. Prospect can be used but it has no good way to deal with ECM rats and will get jammed and its mining hold is smaller. Venture is a good option if you don't have the skills for expedition frigates.

In order of profitability, it is best to prioritize the Hemorphite first, then the Omber and lastly the Jaspet.

All such sites should be dealt with severely and their command structure broken. We do not want a repeat of Kuvakei.

Commander Eliminated

messages: As the bits and pieces from the disintegrated station charge into space, carrying the news of heightened entropy in the universe, your instruments receive an unusual message. It's obviously being transmitted from the Guristas and even though the person on the other end does not introduce himself as such, the special cypher reveals it is indeed theirs. He demands speaking over a secure channel and after you have established one, he continues with sarcastic congratulations on your victory. He then gives you an offer: If you travel to three different locations as he instructs and assassinate the Guristas leaders operating there, he will reward you handsomely. He then gives you coordinates to a location in a "take it or leave it" manner before bidding you farewell and adds that he will contact you after the first target is destroyed.

messages: As the bits and pieces from the disintegrated station charge into space, carrying the news of heightened entropy in the universe, your instruments receive an unusual message. It's obviously being transmitted from the Guristas and even though the person on the other end does not introduce himself as such, the special cypher reveals it is indeed theirs. He demands speaking over a secure channel and after you have established one, he continues with sarcastic congratulations on your victory. He then gives you an offer: If you travel to three different locations as he instructs and assassinate the Guristas leaders operating there, he will reward you handsomely. He then gives you coordinates to a location in a "take it or leave it" manner before bidding you farewell and adds that he will contact you after the first target is destroyed.
The convoy from which you picked up this transmission seems to have left before you got here. Your systems have down traced their new destination.
No ships here and it looks like the Gurista convoy has managed to slip away. You have no clues left to follow.

No ships here and it looks like the Gurista convoy has managed to slip away again. The only possible clue you have is one further location listed in the flight plan, even though by the looks of it they have abandoned it altogether.
No ships here, but it looks like a few ship wrecks have been left behind. You investigate one of them to discover a list of coordinates, one of which is complete and close by.

This was just a supply station like any other usually associated with the large empires and you wonder who it could have possibly been servicing out here in the middle of nowhere. Surely the Guristas have no need for a complex of this size way out here, or do they?

* 2 stasis web towers 31km off. Both web immediately.

Got Chased out before I could finish the site. Will update later when I can. - Kaboose 909

Killed control tower which unlocked the gate

pockets.title: Room 2
pockets.prose:
WARNING! Second room contains 4 siege railguns (80km away) that can hit for 300-400 against a tengu with 62% thermal, 92% kinetic resists! They volley at the same time.

2023.9.17 update

Siege railguns have a damage type of 10% EM, 10% Explosive, 30% Thermal, 50% Kinetic. 

A Proteus with a resistance of 87% Thermal, 95% Kinetic, 50% EM, 10% Explosive, would take 200~350 damage from one hit.

4 siege railguns DO fire at the same time, rate of fire around 15 seconds a shot.

attacking the station will cause a Kinetic smartbomb activation, causing around 6000 Kinetic damage. The smartbomb does not repeat.

When the station is brought down to 20% structure, it would spawn a wave of 20 battleships plus more scram web frigates and a dread guristas conquistador with a 10m isk bounty. It is recommended to use afterburner to avoid damage from battleship torpedos.

If you kill the station and warp out but do not kill the faction spawn, the whole site including the faction commander will despawn.

I recommended killing the scram / web frigates immediately and taking down a couple of the siege rail guns before attacking the station. The DPS from the railguns plus the second wave can quickly overwhelm even a blingy ship.

messages: The station databanks contain information on the Gurista security network and among it; a location of yet another station similar to this one. That is your best clue as to where the ships that fled as you entered have gone.

To your dismay, the main computers of the station took a direct hit during your assault and any information that might have been there has now gone up in smoke. However, your instruments ran through the data from the fleeing ships and have come up with this location as a suggestion to where they might have warped.

It looks like the most interesting of these Gurista ships got away during the fight. Luckily for you though, one of its communication devices seems to be malfunctioning for no apparent reason sending out a constant stream of screeching sounds. Your instruments have no problem tracing where it is coming from. It is an extremely irritating sound. Aggravating too. The screeching of doom.
In local when Dostan is attacked
The pirate station has activated a smartbomb, damaging all hostile ships within range!
In local when Dostan is at 50% armor
The pirate station has called on reinforcements from a nearby deadspace pocket.
In local when Dostan is at 25% armor
In local when Dostan is destroyed
Dini Mator: Noooo! You've just ruined years of research. I can't believe it. You will PAY for that, mongrel!

For a while there, you almost wished you had brought more friends with you and you are relieved you managed to blow the station before more could scramble against you. You are also relieved you managed to kill off that blasted gurgle sound. Permanently.

messages:
The Guristas Pirates, despite being an extremely modern and high-tech faction in their own right, often turn to old tactics to foil their Caldari Navy foes. The most common tactic is to launch a series of guerilla raids -- led by a Dread Guristas Irregular -- on numerous soft targets. State forces become harried and stretched thin, allowing the pirates to carry out their real objectives with minimal inference.

DED Threat Assessment: 3 of 10
So an entire Caldari station is a "soft target"? The DED needs to update its intel.
"Irregular Detected - You have found the Dread Guristas Irregular and its support wing. Kill them all."
"Irregular Destroyed - The Irregular has been eliminated. The State can focus its resources elsewhere. And you can focus on robbing the Irregular's wreckage of valuable prizes."

intro:

The site consists of a volume of space with an acceleration gate and contains various structures and their defending pirates.

This site's acceleration gate allows all subcapitals to enter.

Warning: The DPS in the Second/third rooms becomes quite heavy. Do not attempt this site if you do not know what you are doing or you risk losing your ship quite easily.

pockets.title: Room 1
pockets.prose: All ships will auto-aggro.

rows.name: Acceleration Gate
rows.note: Unlocks when all defenders are dead.

pockets.title: Room 2
pockets.prose: Significant amount of (mostly) kinetic damage in this room. Prioritize battlecruisers and battleships first since their missiles make up most of the incoming damage and have long range.

rows.name: Acceleration Gate
rows.note: Unlocks when all defenders are dead.

pockets.title: Room 3
pockets.prose: Kill Guristas Distributor then either loot his wreck or bookmark it, warp out, and come back a few minutes later to pick up the loot. Triple Stasis Tower spawn will reduce your speed to <10 m/s, making you take a LOT of damage, especially if you rely on speed-tanking.

rows.name: Gurista Distributor
rows.cargo: Contains 18th Tier Overseers Effects, and may contain Pithum B-type cruiser modules, Dread Guristas faction modules and rarely a Gila BPC.

rewards.title: Loot
rewards.text: Possible deadspace modules

messages: These storage areas and warehouses are absolutely full of hallucinogens. It looks like there's a thick layer of additional security between the receiving area and the production facility.
There's the culprit, a Gurista Distributor. It's going to take a long time for these filthy pirates to replace such an integral part of their organization.

"Distributor Down. 
The Gurista distributor's frozen corpse is floating in a cloud of his own product. Given how tough his ship was, there's probably some valuable loot in the wreck."

messages: To your surprise, the Overseer seems to have spent the last moments of his life sending some message to your ship on a private channel, a fact you learn from a blinking entry on your communication panel a few seconds after his innards slid across your windshield, bounced along your fuselage and were sucked into your thrusters. It appears he wanted to save his life by telling you the whereabouts of some place you could load your cargohold with riches, but before he could get very far with his offer, his journey ended. All you have is some hysteric babble about a hidden mining station at a certain location.
More merc ships appear when the Control Tower is attacked.

Either the Overseer was trying to trick you and this was the best he could come up with, or that you killed him before he could reveal the juicy parts of his offer. Either way, the takings from this expedition were as juicy as the good Overseer's remains after your thrusters were done with him.
Among the things you find are a few drones. Running a scan on their control units reveals they have been used not long ago, at another place not far away from here.
It seems this Moon Mining facility has fallen prey to Rogue Drones. The structural makeup of this facility indicates it once belonged to the Guristas.
More drones have been deployed from the Starbase Hangars as the Control Tower is attacked!

All these moon mining stations suggest there must be a station or outpost somewhere in the region servicing them and refining the raw materials they produce. Again you look for clues from the drones, but the data you extract suggests no new locations, only the two you have been at already. If the Guristas have any more stations in the area, this is not where you will find them.

All these moon mining stations suggest there must be a station or outpost somewhere in the region servicing them and refining the raw materials they produce. Again you look for clues from the drones and again the data you extract suggest a new location not too far away.

Going through data scanned during the destruction of the station itself, you notice reports from a place called "R&D division Red", containing information on blueprint research and booster production and even the location of this base "Red".

This Research Station has a built-in defense system. As soon as it is attacked, the inhabitants activate the system, causing a large blast-wave which affects all hostile ships in the vicinity . It is activated continuously until it needs a short delay to recharge power.

Now, you kind of regret killing the Overseer back there, it is always useful to know corrupt leaders who are ready to sell out things like this outpost in exchange for something as cheap as their own petty lives.

The amount of energy harvested and stored here is phenomenal. Exploiting these facilities for your own use might sound tempting, if it weren't for the fact that the entire place is under complete lockdown and only the highest-level Angel security codes will grant access.

You have no idea where to go next. Your name will however not be forgotten by certain Angel commanders.

The amount of energy harvested and stored here is phenomenal. Exploiting these facilities for your own use might sound tempting, if it weren't for the fact that the entire place is under complete lockdown and only the highest-level Angel security codes will grant access.

You did however manage to gain access to an open channel in their communication network, and two energy storage locations were revealed to you.

This facility was not just used for energy storage. Ships, modules and other supplies were storedd in those containers, and sadly every single one was destroyed when the Gurista commanders gave the order. They knew you were coming, and there was little the could do about it on such short notice. The slaughter continues as you prepare to visit the second energy storage facility.

You arrive at the second energy storage facility to find it completely deserted. It looks like the party ended before you arrived. Luckily for youm your computers pick up several signals in the nearby area, one of which seems to have unusually high amounts of combat ships.

pockets.prose:
Do not be fooled by the relative lack of large ships in this pocket; the cruisers deal a significant amount of Kinetic missile damage in excess of 250 DPS with decent application even to smaller ships. Kiting is difficult as their missiles can hit you out past 60 km. Medium drones and larger will have no fun in this pocket as they will draw full room aggro.

Recommended to maximize your Kinetic resistances to at least 70% and run a 10MN Afterburner for cruiser and battlecruiser fits to mitigate some of the damage.

messages:
This small deadspace complex was built by the militant Guristas pirates. It serves as a scout outpost and a minor rendezvous point for reconnaissance teams. 
DED Threat Assessment: Risky (4 of 10)

The scout base perimeter is defended by light spacecraft acting as security for the sensitive recon equipment deeper inside the complex. The security acceleration gate is known to be actively blocked by the security team, allowing no intruders entry while they remain at work.

This section of the complex houses the delicate sensor equipment used to support the Guristas coded communication network. Relay pylons and scout bases surround a small supply depot in the pocket's center, known to contain military supplies and equipment for the reconnaissance arm of the Guristas organization.

Combined damage output will be very high if you aren't careful with pulling room aggro, recommend clearing each group individually. The acceleration gate is locked until all defenders are dead.

messages:
This deadspace complex has been annexed by the Guristas forces to house an entertainment and recuperation center for troops on leave. While the area is not heavily guarded by on-duty personnel, the complex is normally occupied by a wide range of warships and experienced off-duty military staff.
 
DED Threat Assessment: Major (6 of 10)

This entrance pocket of the complex serves as a checkpoint to alert the internal pockets of the complex in the case of any intrusion or a Concord raid.

The acceleration gate leading towards the Recuperation Tower is scrambled by the resident Guristas pilots, making it critical to take out those peripheral defenses before advancing forth.

The so called 'Recuperation Tower' pocket appears to be a sector where Pith Guristas soldiers can rest and help themselves to a drink at the local cantina. It serves as a meeting point for troops coming in with weekend passes, to continue further into the festivities that take place deeper into the complex.

According to intelligence reports, this pocket has been named 'Sin Boulevard' by the mercenaries that frequent this place of degeneracy. It is the central section of the complex and contains the main attraction for visiting members of the Guristas army. The acceleration gate leading deeper into the complex is for high-rollers only, being a hub for gambling and bloodsport events.

The final sector of the reinvigoration camp houses casinos and a large arena for pitching involuntary captives of the Pith Guristas against each other in violent bloodsport events. According to intelligence reports this pocket contains the greatest military might within the complex, being such a strong attraction for the wealthy and world-weary officers of the mercenary league.

"As you enter the room, you receive a weak transmission; a hushed voice sneaks through your audio system, hastily whispering some words. All you can understand is something about kidnapping, pirates and a group of people. You play it back a several times, trying to make sense of it, but you can not discern who is kidnapped or how this group of people is involved and you cant actually hear what part the Guristas play in this, even though you take it for granted that they are the kidnappers in question. This message was sent on a general channel and your instruments have no problem pinpointing its origin. They have actually done so already in case you would like to investigate this further. Cant beat these new auto-personalizing AI systems, you have had this one for only a few days and it already feels like it has known you all your life."

messages:
As one of the most well-organized and opportunistic outfits inside the Guristas, the H-PA Crew were not caught unaware when synth booster production and sale was legalized inside Empire space. They quickly finalized their own preparations and set out in small jump freighter gangs from the core Venal system where they had first earned a name for themselves. Their goal was to be the primary supplier in and around Caldari space for anyone seeking the enhanced form of the same Blue Pill and Crash boosters that were now flowing freely across all empire-sanctioned markets.

They figured that capsuleers and other spacefaring clients would likely want the improved versions once they realized the limitations of synth booster variants. Their estimation hasn't proved wrong and these days the H-PA narco-squads are very well funded.

messages: You pick up a signal containing co-ordinates to a mysterious location. Surely, True Creations are up to something.

All you find are a few bits and pieces of ancient machinery and a couple of hollow structures. Marks on the floating objects and some of the debris floating around, hints to this place having recently been excavated. You have however no means of finding out by whom or where they might be by now.

All you find are a few bits and pieces of ancient machinery and a couple of hollow structures. However, your instruments identify this place as one of two locations specially registered as "digs" in a database picked up from one of the ship wrecks. You set destination for the other location.

Despite the Sansha's heroic effort to throw you off track, your instruments manage to gather enough information before the main force escapes too far away. They left before you got there, but you still know where they're heading.

The fleeing ships are long gone and at first this seems to be a dead end. The place you have found here is yet another depleted dig of an ancient Sansha settlement and it seems like work was finished here not long ago and that whoever was digging here has left behind quite a lot of old equipment. While snooping around a bit, you find delivery records for food and household items stating they were sent to here from another nearby location.

You have stopped one group of Sanshas engaged in bolstering the revival of their Nation by digging up what is left of their old fame and riches. But you are sure there are many groups like them digging in hundreds of dark corners in the galaxy, all awaiting the triumphant return of the Sansha Nation among the empires.

DED deep space scouts briefly explored this strange site and left behind a rather cryptic note. As far as you can tell some ancient ruins lie within, but who built them or what treasures might lie buried there are anyone's guess.
As you come out of acceleration you notice the resemblance of a spatial rift in the distance.
Core Relay Commander: They've found the portal! Destroy them before they escape!
Upon attacking the Core Relay Commander
As the Relay Commander is attacked, he calls for backup! More hostile ships are incoming!
Upon attacking the Core Relay Commander
As the Relay Commander is attacked, he calls for backup! More hostile ships are incoming!

A large force of drones has taken up residence in this area. They obviously benefit greatly from salvaging the remnants of the former inhabitants, which still litters this patch of space. A drone presence this large could not be formed without an abundance of raw materials.
Upon destroying one of the missile batteries
Drones have been deployed from the Drone Bunkers in response to the attack on the sentry guns!
Someone has triggered an ancient land mine! All ships inside the blast radius take damage.

The source of the drone infestation seems to lie in this deadspace pocket, located inside a fiery nebula. The extreme and hostile environment, accompanied by a very heavy drone presence, seems to have kept most of the looters away, as two fully intact ancient ruins would indicate.
The Drone Hive Mother has deployed Drone Cruise Missile Batteries along with more drone ships!
Drones have emerged from the nearby bunkers to defend the Hive Mother!
Drones have emerged from the nearby bunkers to defend the Hive Mother!
Drones have emerged from the nearby bunkers to defend the Hive Mother!
In local (upon destroying the Hive Mother)

The Hive Mother has been eliminated, and the buzz of drone communications slowly calms down. Some drones machines may still be active, but at least their numbers will no longer be replenished by the frenzied replication process inside the Drone Mother.
Someone has gone too close to one of the ruins and triggered an ancient hidden explosive. Energy and material spurts in all directions, and all ships caught in the blast radius take damage!

Hierarchy.name: Hierarchy
intro:
Hierarchy is an Unrated Complex found in nullsec via exploration.

Video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZOGyRqx4Emo Gila]

The site is behind an acceleration gate. Warping to the site lands you at 0 on the gate. All rats must be cleared to activate the acceleration gate to the second room.

blocks.title: Gate spawn after approaching acceleration gate

pockets.title: Second Room
pockets.prose:
Blitz: 
The entire site has no warp disruptors or scrams so most rats can be ignored if you can tank them.
Upon landing approach the Warning Sign near the Hierarchy structure. Getting close will trigger the first spawn.
Each new wave is triggered by simply damaging a single rat so you can quickly spawn the battleship wave. 
Kill all the battleships, spawning the Sentient, kill it, bookmark the wreck and warp off. After the site has despawned grab your loot and possibly salvage the wreck (average 9-11m in Salvage).

messages: At the beginning of this fight, your instruments picked up a distress call from a drone squadron not too far away, supposedly meant for the hive you just destroyed. The messenger was calling in combat assistance, including identification marks, information on what he was fighting and the location. The weird thing is that this is obviously a drone messaging and claiming he is being attacked by some other drones...

Inside is nothing, but you will get either an escalation or DEAD END.

Warping to this stage places you in a cloud around 20-30km from the nearest enemy ships. Bookmarking the location will allow you to warp to any distance you choose.

There is a chance the escalation will end after this site.

pockets.title: Area 1
pockets.prose: Activate the acceleration gate.

pockets.title: Area 2
pockets.prose: The escalation will either end here, or continue.

notes.title: Hired Gun Part 3

notes.title: Hired Gun Part 4

messages: As you decimate the last remnants of this rogue drone base, your sensors come across some old transportation data; lists of materials, modules, ships and locations. The only reason this is a kind of odd is that rogue drones usually are very self sufficient, making in situ what they need for their colonies. Perhaps this is nothing...

Arriving at the most recent location in the files, you come across a blown out rogue drone hive, someone must have been here before you. Thankfully there are a couple of other locations in those files that make any sense to your navigation systems, the closer one being...
Arriving at the only recognizable location in the files you found, you come across a blown out rogue drone hive. Whatever this once was, it obviously is no more....

Arriving at one of the remaining locations in the files, you come across a blown out rogue drone hive, someone must have been here before you. There is one other location here that makes any sense to your navigation systems.
Well, that was a surprise. Rogue drones, turned carebears and mining their cogs off! Why? Perhaps this navigational beacon will lead you to some answers.

Well, that was a surprise. Rogue drones, turned carebears and mining their cogs off! Why? Perhaps this navigational beacon could have lead you to some answers, but it seems to have been damaged in the heat of battle.

Rogue drones mining and gathering resources far and wide to supply a huge drone factory! This scale of operations does not seem to fit anything you have seen or heard about them before and this level of organization kind of takes the "rogue" out of "rogue drones". You are pretty sure that somewhere, some authority would love to get a report on this. But on second thought... all the paperwork involved would probably be enough to exhaust a black hole.

It is very hard and should only be attempted by skilled players. CONCORD and Amarr Empire rats are present. You will likely receive hefty standing losses from them. 
AVOID using cap-dependent modules in this site, you will likely lose your ship.

messages: Among the debris from this formidable hive, you find a blown out hangar containing a few burnt out space ships of various types, probably the possessions of some unfortunate adventurers that came here before you and didn't live to tell the story. As your scanners routinely run through this material, they come across some report with information on a few sister hives to this one. The explorer seems to have found that each of these so called 'independence hives' are surrounded with outposts that serve both as an early warning system against intruders on the drones territory and also as a resource gathering facility. It seems that if the hive is attacked, the drones from the outpost warp instantly back to defend it. One interesting bit of information the unfortunate explorer has noted is that the drones frequently move the hive itself between these outposts, so hunting these things is like playing Russian roulette, you never know if you are fortunate enough to hit an outpost and thereby reduce the inevitable resistance at the main hive or if you are warping straight into the lair of the drones. The report continues to list four locations, the nearest one being...

Scarcity Update: This site, like other cosmic signatures, contains ore.
* As of 1st March 2021 the site contains large amounts of Hedbergite & Hemorphite, with smaller amounts of Omber, Kernite and ores found in high sec. The ore spans a crescent shape of 120km across and is therefore impossible to scan with a single survey. It was estimated on approximately a third of the belt scanned that ISK value at current prices would be 2.5-3b. Note that if the site is left by all players it may despawn, but leaving one player at all times within the site will retain it in space for mining.
* As of 3rd March 2021 the only asteroids showing on overview at the site were Scordite and Veldspar. Very disappointing.
* As of 15th of October 2021 the site, once again, contains only large amounts of Scordite and Veldspar.

Each pair of first reinforcements will spawn a new pair of same type.

Finishing reinforcement 2 spawns reinforcement 3. This group spawns around 100 km from warp-in.
DO NOT KILL REINFORCEMENT 3!

Killing reinforcement 3 triggers massive enemy wave. These ships will close in very quickly and will web and point. You will not be match for them.
The ships have special types: "Temko Interceptor", "COSMOS Gallente Commodore", "Cosmos Gallente Elite Frigate" and "Cosmos Gallente Captain". They were easily able to overpower a Vargur with 1700 ehp/s tank.

pockets.title: Fourth location
pockets.prose:
Single normal space pocket.

This last site is not time-sensitive, though it can be time-consuming if you do not bring something that can tank the high DPS or snipe the three Madcat Frigates from afar. Once the three Madcats are killed, the container unlocks. The loot can be anything from Metal Scraps to the usual array of faction modules.

The Madcat Frigates are effectively a DPS check, as they boast high passive shield regeneration, strong 90% armor resistances, and strong armor repair. Fortunately, you do not need that much DPS (at least 180) to kill them if you pull them away from the site, though more is always better. While it is much faster to be able to overwhelm their armor repair, it is not strictly necessary. Recommend at least 450 DPS to break their active tank. 

Note - Apr 2025: It seems that there is some criteria under which they stop repairing their armor. I can't figure out what it is, and it doesn't seem to be consistent. It allowed me to kill 2/3 of the Madcat frigates, but not the third.

August 2026: Madcats destroyed with HAMs and a Web.

For clearing this site, there are three approaches: bookmark chaining to kite, sniping, or tanking. 

For the first two approaches (kiting/sniping), all you have to do is warp in, then warp out to the sun (or somewhere consistent) after creating a bookmark. Then, you warp to your bookmark at the site at 100km, and then create another bookmark so you are now 200km from the site. Depending on if you are kiting or sniping, you may be able to stop here and pick off the 5 Sentry Guns who can do a fair amount of damage up to 250km. However, if you can't, then you'll need to repeat the process one more time so you're 250-300km from the site. Then, you'll need to warp into the site at 0, tag an enemy once (or more, depending on your fit and tank), and then warp out to your bookmark at 250-300km. Provided you managed to shoot an enemy, they should aggro and begin moving toward you, even if you temporarily break the lock via warping to 300km. For the Madcats, this process won't take very long thanks to their MWDs. For the other rats, however, this can be a time-consuming process if not using a ship able to hit 100-250km (such as a cheap Railgun Naga, for example), as their speed is a painful 300-500 m/s.

Once the Madcats are dead, you can warp straight to the cargo container for the loot, and then leave. If you're unlucky, you'll only get a single Metal Scrap. If you're lucky, you can receive Coreli A-type modules.

[More information needed for minimum tanking requirements here]

Structures on site

Note that the reinforcement spawn appears to vary to some degree, as one user reported 9 additional enemies spawning in addition to the 10 battlecruisers.

Despite the fact that you have no sister that you know of and the guy sounds like he has been drinking more than just Quafe, you feel a certain temptation to go and see what this is all about.
Serpentis Madcat: Well look at who we have here boys, looks like a garbage hauler. I wonder what nincompoop decided to send him out here through our turf. Maybe his mother? Ha ha.
Serpentis Madcat: I've had enough fun with this freak, I doubt he has anything worth looting. Let's roll boys!
Heuristic analysis of this location indicates that destroying the Serpentis Armory would greatly improve your odds of uncovering further illicit activity

These seem to be just some Serp rich kids on Crash looking for trouble, rather than serious bloodthirsty pirates. In some jet set ships, probably with modules to die for.., in any case your instruments have an easy lock on their destination in case you have nothing more important to do than to spank those brats.

These seem to be just some brats on Crash looking for trouble, rather than serious bloodthirsty pirates. In some jet set ships, probably with modules to die for.., in any case your instruments are unable to determine their destination.
These seem to be just some punks on drugs looking for trouble rather than bloodthirst pirates. In any case, your instruments have an easy lock on their destination.
It seems like you have the choices of staying here and getting murdered by the Angel babysitters, or you could try to jet out and see if the lock you have on the rest of the brats is any good...
Finally! Your navigation panel proudly flashes a suggested destination for the Serpentis brats.

Serpentis Madcat: That's it! You have the audacity to enter the proximity of our Pleasure Resorts! I can't lose face in front of the girls inside ... I mean I can't let you get away with that! ... Prepare to die, pest.

Your computers pick up distress signals being sent from somewhere in the area. Perhaps this indicates that more enemy ships may be incoming soon. Whatever you're after here, you should probably make haste before you are overwhelmed.

Killing rich kids may be lucrative, but when they have an army of hard core Guardian Angels to hold their hand like this, it can be a bit troublesome. These at least will have enough to talk about in their luxury clone bay tonight, wherever that may be.
