messages: As you enter the room, you receive a weak transmission; a hushed voice sneaks through your audio system, hastily whispering some words. All you can understand is something about kidnapping, pirates and a group of people. You play it back a several times, trying to make sense of it, but you can not discern who is kidnapped or how this group of people is involved and you cant actually hear what part the Guristas play in this, even though you take it for granted that they are the kidnappers in question. This message was sent on a general channel and your instruments have no problem pinpointing its origin. They have actually done so already in case you would like to investigate this further. Cant beat these new auto-personalizing AI systems, you have had this one for only a few days and it already feels like it has known you all your life.
grrble grbble gurista taken away....left beacon...no power. rescue us

While investigating the wreck, you suddenly receive the same transmission as before, but this time in much better quality. Soon you discover that this is actually a message recorded on some children's toy that utilizes small shiny plastic discs as a storage medium. This message must have been running for some time, as the transmitter has almost run out of power.

After playing the message again and analyzing it in depth, you can now hear that the speaker is describing an attack and that she, along with a group of people have been kidnapped by a locally known Gurista bandit. Either this happened so long ago that this pirate has relocated, or perhaps you just don't know the area well enough. In any case, you have no idea where to go to rescue these people.

You find no sign of any hostages and you are pretty sure that if they had been in the bunker, you would have noticed some body parts being thrown around when you blew it up. You notice that all the ships and the buildings are marked with some sort of a logo, depicting a triangle with glowing corners in different colors and everything encircled with a band of I´s and O´s. You have never seen exactly this one before, but it reminds you of badges some of the more pretentious pirate chiefs you have met have used to bolster their image. After your main computer has had a few seconds to munch on this graphic, it suggests that this symbolizes three locations, one which you are at now and two others, the I´s and O´s seem to be the coordinates to all three locations in binary, the only problem is that there is no indication where on the circle to start reading. But it seems like your instruments have found some reason to make an educated guess and come up with two unexplored locations, the nearer one of the two being...
Another puny little station and now you were absolutely sure there were not hostages or anyone else for that matter inside the bunker when it blew. They must be in the other station!

If ending the hostages plight was the objective, this is definitely a case of "mission accomplished" and as the people who would most energetically refute that statement are eternally indisposed, you should have little problems feeling good about yourself.
In local chat after destroying Conquered Station - 'Fatal Rabbit'

Ships AI Message: Hi Captain! In the explosion you have obliterated not only the station, the kidnapping gurista but also the people you tried to rescue. Whoopsy! Let´s hope they have found release in death. I do not recommend collecting the body parts because it will stink and extra energy will then be required to make this vessel habitable.

It looks as if you have surprised the drones while pillaging the remains of this asteroid colony. Again you can see bodies floating around, even some children toys... You don't know who these people were, but no one deserves this tragic and violent end from the "hands" of the machines. You can only hope you have found the rest of the drones connected to this hive so the people in the region may be safe from the drone menace for a while at least...

Mare_Sargassum.name: Mare Sargassum

pockets.title: Part 1
pockets.prose:
----

The initial defenders can vary wildly.

The initial defenders consists of around 6 frigates and one sentient drone.
* Note: Trash Construction is not vulnerable (despite warp-in message) - just approach it to trigger reinforcement wave. (On 26-Nov-YC124 destroying elite frigates didn't trigger reinforcement wave.)

Reinforcement wave triggers when the elite frigates are destroyed. It is possible to have this wave included in initial defenders, possibly due to warping through the trash construct.

Two additional spawns triggered by killing ships from initial spawn

rows.name: Sentient Alvi
rows.cargo: Drone components, can also drop Astero chip

pockets.title: Part 2
pockets.prose:
----
There is at least one reinforcement wave. The escalation can be triggered by killing either the Sentient drone, or all enemies except the Sentient drone.

rows.name: Sentient Shatter/... Alvior
rows.cargo: Drone components or Astero chip

pockets.title: Part 3
pockets.prose:
----
Fewer rogue drones, and killing the sentient drone once again triggered the escalation. As a bonus, you get to see a great big red cube in space. The Borg turned more evil?

rows.name: Sentient Ripper/... Alvior
rows.cargo: Drone components or Astero chip

pockets.title: Part 4
pockets.prose:
----
This part may be in a low-sec system (26 Feb 2017 ended in a .5 system / 26 Apr 2017 ended in .6 system / 26 Aug 2019 ended in a .3 system / 9 Dec 2019 ended in a .5 system / 3 Sep 2020 ended in a .2 system / 18 Mar 2024 ended in Ahbazon / 9 Nov 2024 ended in a .5 system).

5 small rogue drones waiting on warpin, and 5 "Drone Hold" cans. Completion popup happened after blowing up the first wave and starting to open cans. Strain Splinter drones can warp scram and web. Two reinforcement waves later appeared, one with a Rogue Mining Overseer dropping T2 salvage. One of the Drone Hold cans contained some drone goo (Dark Compound, Condensed Compound). All drone hold cans can be empty.

rows.name: Rogue Mining Overseer
rows.cargo: T2 Salvage

notes.title: Overview
notes.text:
Mare Sargassum is an expedition found by completing Desolate Site combat sites. It may contain up to four parts. The first three will be in high-sec space, while the fourth can be in low-sec or high-sec.
The sites do not have gates, and can be easily completed in a cruiser.

rewards.title: Rewards
rewards.text: Each part has a commander rat which, when killed, will drop T2 salvage and Rogue Drone components. Lootable cans may contain drone alloys.

messages: At first it seems strange the drones have picked this barren and resource deficient place to build a new hive. But then again, while you were blowing up the place, you noticed a few vessels that might have been used as transports, indicating the drones were pulling in the materials they needed from someplace else. As to compliment you on your reasoning, your communication systems start indicating several different incoming transmissions in drone beeps and clicks and after a while you manage to coerce your instruments into pointing out an approximate spatial origin of the message.
Heuristic analysis of this location indicates that attacking the Trash Construction would greatly improve your odds of uncovering further illicit activity.
All the drones have been obliterated, no clues are offered on where more can be found and your expedition seems to have come to a dead end.

Most of the drones have been obliterated, but a few made it away. Luckily the average drone operates in part like a jukebox trying to play all its tracks repeatedly at the same time over the airwaves, relying on the other drones to filter out the information they need and disregard the rest. Therefore they are usually easy to find while within reasonable range and this time is no different. Your instruments concentrate on messages from one of the escaped drones and after having filtered through several thousand repetitions of electrical manuals for every hydraulic system built the last three hundred years this side of the Myridian Strip, the entire known literature on the theory of relativity recited three times and for some obscure reason a text on the effect of oriental gardening on the human condition played simultaneously on four parallel channels, they finally come across a new location
Drone Signal: Location ðrzs found, location þeðy alerted.
The current strategy chosen by the drones seems to be running away as fast as they can. Your instruments have no problems tracking their destination

The current strategy chosen by the drones seems to be running away as fast as they can in every conceivable direction. For a while you are getting transmissions from all over the place and your tracking devices try desperately to make sense of all this information, but all of a sudden all waves are quiet and you realize that the drones deception has succeeded, you have no clue where to go to hunt them.

You notice that all of these cans bear the markings of the same space station. After checking in your databanks, you find that this particular station was destroyed decades ago and has remained deserted ever since. You retrieve the location...

As expected, the drones were busy turning this old station into a hive, which if they had succeeded would no doubt be spewing out innumerable copies of their kind to haunt this part of the constellation for years to come. You wonder if sentient machines can dream...if so, then this one is at least permanently broken.

Medical_Twilight.name: Medical Twilight
intro: Medical Twilight is an expedition that can be obtained by running Blood Watch combat sites. It will take you to several new systems, each about 4 jumps from the previous one. Only the escalation trigger ship needs to be killed to continue the escalation.

rows.name: Dark Blood Engraver
rows.cargo: Faction loot or blueprint

rows.name: Dark Blood Templar
rows.cargo: Faction loot or blueprint

notes.title: Second pocket
notes.text: Rocks and structures. No pirates.

rewards.title: Rewards
rewards.text: Completing all four escalations gives the possibility of a Cruor BPC or Corpii (Frigate) A-Type module drops in the final escalation site.

escalation.title: First escalation
escalation.text:
The next wave will spawn upon attacking the Ritual Center.

The final wave will spawn when the Ritual Center is at half shield.

Do not underestimate the final wave. Being neuted, pointed and webbed can get you killed quickly! A suggested tactic is to fight at range and only go in to brawl when the elite frigates are off the field. To blitz this site, shoot the Ritual Center until all waves are spawned and then take out the elite frigates followed by the Dark Blood frigate. Be prepared to tank DPS under neut pressure.

escalation.title: Fourth escalation (Lowsec|Highsec)
escalation.text: The warp in is within neut range of the Elite Cruisers. The DPS combined with the heavy neuting and webs is a serious problem for active tanked ships. Dropping a bookmark and warping in at range to the bookmark is recommended. Warping inside the site itself is possible and there are plenty of small asteroids to warp between. You can draw the Blood Factory Overseer and the Elite Frigates away from the rest by kiting (the Overseer BS has a top speed of 700+ m/s). [Jan 2025 (0.5 System)]

escalation.title: Escalation failure
escalation.text: Another Blood hideout and more slaves. You find no clues as to where the medical facility is, nor can you find any information on other parts of this Blood operation. It looks like your expedition has come to an end.

messages: The slaves you liberated from this Blood facility report that this was a holding place where slaves were gathered, before being sent off to a blood replenishing "medical" station. You have heard about those places; where the Blood members go to get their blood exchanged with the blood of a slave who has been put on a special "blood cleansing" diet for a period of time. Needless to say, this leaves the poor slave empty of the vital fluid in question. Understandably your newfound slaves are quite thrilled with these recent turn of events. None of them knows where this so called "medical" station is, but a couple can tell you that they were in another holding station like this one, before they came here and coincidentally it is not all that far away ...
The inhabitants of the Ritual Center have sent out distress signals. and more ships quickly arrive!

The Overseer of the Ritual Center has undocked.
The Ritual Center has deployed sentry guns and more ships into the fray.

Another Blood hideout and more slaves. You find no clues as to where the medical facility is, but piecing together information from the slaves, you are pretty sure some part of this Blood operations is located here ...
This place is long deserted and when your instruments scan the outposts docking station, it turns up logs that are a couple of years old. It seems the blood trail has grown cold.

This place seems to be deserted and recently so, as all systems are up and running. Your scanners can even pick up signals from small houshold appliances, indicating that someone should actually be home. When your instruments scan the outposts docking station, it turns up logs only few minutes old showing four ships departing at the same time, these logs are incomplete though, only listing departure time and destination. For some reason all the ships are headed for the same spot ...

As you float among the debris of the pirate ships you notice several small canisters of ectoplasm, all marked with a place of origin, presumably the Blood's so called 'medical' facility. Whether it is carelessness, cockiness or plain old stupidity is hard to say, but these pirates didn't bother to hide where they came from. Then again, this might be another ambush ...

You are pretty sure that at some time in history, there would have been places in the galaxy where destroying an evil thing like this would have prompted some noble and decent ruler to award you with a medal or even a prize.

Menacing_Mechanics.name: Menacing Mechanics

pockets.title: First Location
pockets.prose:
----
Single pocket containing drone and Guristas ships.

Second wave is triggered without killing anything. Either timed spawn or after agressing.

Wave 3 is triggeres by killing the commander battlecruiser.

rows.name: Sentient Defeater Alvatis
rows.cargo: Rogue Drone 43-X Nexus Chip, Rogue Drone Components

pockets.title: Second Location
pockets.prose:
----
Single pocket.

rows.name: Sentient striker Alvatis
rows.cargo: Rogue Drone 43-X Nexus Chip (Some Times drops)

pockets.title: Third Location
pockets.prose:
----
Single pocket.

Wave 2 is triggered by killing all ships from initial defenders.

rows.name: Sentient Siege Alvatis
rows.cargo: Rogue drone components, possible Sentient faction module/s or Rogue Drone 43-X Nexus Chip

pockets.title: Fourth Location
pockets.prose:
----
Single pocket with drone and mercenary ships. None of the destructible structures seem to trigger or drop anything.

Initial defender information incomplete

rows.name: Rogue Drone Liaisons Captain
rows.cargo: T2 salvage

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text: Unlike many escalations, rats from different pirate factions are present here.

messages:
This drone operation was so small that it could hardly be called a "hive", there were no substantial assembly plants or other major factories here. It looked more like a maintenance station, something that does not rhyme with what you have heard about drones and how they operate, as they usually are confined to self sufficient hives and perhaps operating small resource gathering satellite ops. But a drone maintenance station, servicing several other hives or passersby is almost unheard of. After scanning through the remaining debris, your instruments gather some service logs, further supporting the idea this was an open maintenance station.

Most of the serviced ships seem to have been standard drone vessels, but you can also see some entries naming ships used by humans, even though it does not say anything about who was flying them. Some of the log entries contain extra notes on these customers and among them you find something that looks like coordinates in a system not too far away.

This was probably the smallest Gurista hideout you ever saw and no wonder they were forced from time to time to get their ships serviced elsewhere, even though it was by rogue drones. The mystery is how they managed to get in there and out again in one piece. Usually rogue drones have only one standard response to the sighting of a carbon based life form and that is to run the "murderous rampage" script, or whatever it is that makes them go bonkers in a company where not all members are not purely held together by nuts and bolts. 
While this has been happening, your instruments have been analyzing the drone logs and the next location which shows any promise is already flashing on one of the panels.

This was probably the smallest Gurista hideout you ever saw and no wonder they were forced from time to time to get their ships serviced elsewhere, even though it was by rogue drones. The mystery is how they managed to get in there and out again in one piece. Usually rogue drones have only one standard response to the sighting of a carbon based life form and that is to run the "murderous rampage" script, or whatever it is that makes them go bonkers in a company where not all members are not purely held together by nuts and bolts.
Your systems can not find any further information of value in the drone logs.
Another small pirate camp, this time the Sansha. The next location is lined up, who knows what you will find there...
Heuristic analysis of this location indicates that destroying the Bunker would greatly improve your odds of uncovering further illicit activity.
Mesage on local once bunkers are destroyed.
Drone Signal to Hive: Location #5423 destroyed

Again pirates and this time Angels. It looks like the drones little operation has allowed evil doers from several different factions to reach further away from home than usual. There is one more location available from the drone logs...

Off all the evident customers, a rogue mercenary band was perhaps the least surprising consumers of the drone's services, but still, it is troubling to see any outlaw group being able to cooperate like this with a rogue drone colony.

Mindflood.name: Mindflood
intro: Mindflood is an expedition found by completing Serpentis Hideout signatures. It contains four parts, each of which will be 4-8 jumps from the previous system, in high sec space (though the route may include lowsec).

rows.name: Shadow Serpentis Scout
rows.cargo: Shadow ammunition

rows.name: Shadow Serpentis Scout
rows.cargo: Shadow ammunition

rows.name: Shadow Serpentis Patroller
rows.cargo: Shadow ammunition

pockets.title: Part 4
pockets.prose: In this part there is no acceleration gate, and no Shadow spawn. Destroy the first wave to bring the commander. Erinn will repair armour at around 30-40 DPS.

rows.name: Elgur Erinn
rows.cargo: Coreli C-type modules

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text:
Sites are not gated, and can be completed in a T1 frigate at range, though larger ships will be safer. The final named frigate requires around 50 DPS. In all sections, killing the Shadow Serpentis named frigate will trigger the next phase. If using a T1 frigate, a Tristan and proper range is highly recommended.

In the second room in each phase there is usually Elgur Erinn escorted by two frigates and they will warp away immediately.

rewards.title: Rewards
rewards.text:
Each part has a commander rat which, when killed, will drop faction ammunition and Shadow Serpentis tags. Typical module drop includes a Vortex Compact Magnetic Field Stabilizer. The commander may also drop implants, e.g. Mid-grade Snake Beta (and possibly Shadow Serpentis modules by comparison with other escalations, but not seen). Salvaging commander wrecks may generate T2 salvage.

Elgur Erinn may drop Coreli C-Type modules.

messages: Either your sensors are malfunctioning or the data was incorrect. The Serpentis ships are nowhere to be seen.
Your sensors pick up on the Serpentis trail and provide you with a set of coordinates to their next probable destination.

Minmatar_Contracted_Bio-Farm.name: Minmatar Contracted Bio-Farm
intro:
Minmatar Contracted Bio-Farm is a DED Rated Complex. It can be found by scanning cosmic signatures in Minmatar high security space.

The entry to this site is limited to T2 and Faction frigates and below.

pockets.title: Room 1
pockets.prose:
Upon activating the acceleration gate to the room.

The acceleration gate to the second room is locked and requires Thorak’s Private Key. The key is in Thorak's Biodome Garden.

rows.name: Thorak's Biodome Garden
rows.cargo: Thorak’s Private Key and 1st Tier Overseer's Personal Effects.

rows.name: Acceleration Gate
rows.note: Requires Thorak's Private Key. It is consumed on use.

pockets.title: Room 2
pockets.prose: Upon activating the acceleration gate to the room.

rows.name: Oofus's Repair Shop
rows.cargo: 2nd Tier Overseer's Personal Effects and may contain Gistii C-type modules, Angel Cartel faction modules or a Dramiel BPC.

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text:
Upon warping to the beacon.

This is a two room complex.

rewards.title: Loot
rewards.text:
Example loot 2024-01-07 (excluding overseer effects):

Gistii C-Type Small Remote Shield Booster

Salvage: 759k

Normal Modules/Ammunition: 68k

messages: Somewhat surprisingly, the Angel Cartel contracted the building of experimental celestial biofarms from the Minmatar Republic. Clouds made of organic dust and water-based asteroids make this experiment possible.
Ironically, slave trade is rampant in this Minmatar contracted biodome complex. Thorak is a ruthless businessman, turned politician, and his future in a galactic context looks bright.

A major blow was dealt to an otherwise successful energy pooling operation when a meteor shower pummeled the control bridge to pieces. Reports indicate that Orfus, the CEO of the the self-titled galactic repair corporation, agreed to fix it for the troubled energy contractor in return for huge stakes in the eventual profits.

Minor_Angel_Annex.name: Minor Angel Annex
intro:
Minor Angel Annex is an unrated Complex occupied by the Angel Cartel pirate faction. It can be found by probing in Lowsec. Its signal strength is 10%, making it moderately easy to scan down.

The site is accessed through an acceleration gate. While a well fit battlecruiser can solo the first part, it would be difficult if not impossible to do so for the second part. This complex is unrated and is of a difficulty similar to a 5 or 6/10 DED Rated Complexes

pockets.title: First room
pockets.prose:
More defenders appear as the communications officers are agressed. The militant commander appears in last wave. The destruction of militant commander unlocks the acceleration gate.
The wave information here is inaccurate and should be considered as a rough view of the site.

pockets.title: Second room
pockets.prose:
The information of waves in second room is even worse than for first room.

The second wave seems to be triggered by sentries. Supervisor is triggered by attacking the drug factory. Attacking the drug factory may trigger all other waves too if they have not been triggered before engaging the station. Commander is triggered by killing the supervisor. Other triggers are unknown.

To engage next wawe hit the drug farm

rows.name: Domination
rows.cargo: Can drop faction module, implant or BPC.

rewards.title: Loot
rewards.text:
*Bounty: Approx 7 M ISK in the first room, 10 M ISK in the second room
*Loot and Salvage: Approx 6 - 8 M ISK in the first room, 6 - 8 M ISK in the second rooom
*The Domination ship has a chance to drop faction or Gist mods.

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.text: This site may escalate to Angel Owned Station.

messages: Previous explorers have commented that one of the gates requires a passkey. Alternatively, it can be bypassed by convincing the commander to unlock it. The overseer guards the drug farm vigorously.

Minor_Blood_Annex.name: Minor Blood Annex
intro: Minor Blood Annex is a low security unrated site found through exploration. Excercise extreme caution due to multiple waves potentially having been spawned before you enter.

pockets.title: 1st pocket
pockets.prose:
The webbing drone in each group will spawn the next group. On some occasions multiple groups will already be present when you warp in.
In final wave the destruction of Corpus Militant Commander unlocks the gate.
The gate can also be unlocked with a Blood Crystal Tag. The tag is consumed.

pockets.title: 2nd pocket
pockets.prose:
Destroying the webbing drones will again trigger additional waves.
Attacking the cathedral triggers cathedral wave.
Destroying Corpus Militant Supervisor in cathedral wave triggers commander wave.

rows.name: Dark Blood Seer
rows.cargo: Can drop faction items.

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text: Upon warping to the site you will arrive at an acceleration gate.

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.text: The site can escalate to Blood Owned Station.

messages: Previous explorers have commented that one of the gates requires a passkey. Alternatively, it can be bypassed by convincing the commander to unlock it. The overseer guards the Cathedral vigorously.

Minor_Conduit.name: Minor Conduit
intro:
This combat anomaly is found when a system is either leaning towards the Triglavian Collective or the EDENCOM forces. It is a harder and more advanced version of the Emerging Conduit site.

They contain 5 waves of Triglavian NPCs containing 12-15 ships in each.

Clearing this site helps the EDENCOM forces.

Minor_Guristas_Annex.name: Minor Guristas Annex
intro: The Minor Guristas Annex is an Unrated Complex found by scanning in Low Security regions with Guristas presence.

pockets.title: First Pocket
pockets.prose: Either kill the Pith Militant Commander to unlock the acceleration gate or use a Guristas Crystal Tag to proceed into the second room.

pockets.title: Second Pocke t
pockets.prose: Large amount of ECM in this room.

rows.name: Weapons Manufacturing Plant
rows.trigger: Attacking aggros all ships. Triggers Supervisor wave when attacked.

rows.name: Pith Militant Supervisor(Pith Massacrer)
rows.trigger: Destruction completes site, and triggers commander wave
rows.note: Higher active shield tank than other NPCs

rows.name: Dread Guristas Executor
rows.cargo: Possible Dread Guristas faction modules or implants

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text:
This site is very similar to Guristas Watch. Recommended high resists for kinetic and thermal damage.

Video: [[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tk_hO76WXOI HAM Tengu] February 2014]

Upon warping to the signature you will land at an acceleration gate.

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.text: Can escalate to Guristas Owned Station

messages: The Pith Communications Officer has called on reinforcements to save his own hide!
The Pith Communications Officer has called on reinforcements to save his own hide!
Pith Militant Commander: The Overseer will have us all made into biomass burgers for the Sansha if we don't keep those intruders from the weapons manufacturing plant! Get them!
The Pith Communications Officer has called on reinforcements to save his own hide!
In local when Pith Militant Commander is destroyed
The wreckage of the Pith Militant Commander's ship reveals access codes that allow you to unlock the acceleration gate. Proceed through with caution!
A number of Pith ships have answered the distress signals sent by the Pith Transmitter!
In local(upon attacking Weapons Manufacturing Plant)
Pith Militant Overseer: Incompetent mongrels. Must I do everything myself around here?
In local when timed spawn appears
A number of Pith ships have answered the distress signals sent by the Pith Long-Range Transmitter.

To your surprise, the Overseer seems to have spent the last moments of his life sending some message to your ship on a private channel, a fact you learn from a blinking entry on your communication panel a few seconds after his innards slid across your windshield, bounced along your fuselage and were sucked into your thrusters. It appears he wanted to save his life by telling you the whereabouts of some place you could load your cargohold with riches, but before he could get very far with his offer, his journey ended. All you have is some hysteric babble about a hidden mining station at a certain location.

Minor_Sansha_Annex.name: Minor Sansha Annex
intro: Minor Sansha Annex is an Unrated Complex found by scanning in Low Security systems in Sansha infested space.

pockets.title: First Pocket
pockets.prose: Approach the acceleration gate to trigger the proximity wave.

blocks.title: Initial defenders (2 Groups, both ~30km from warp-in)

rows.name: Acceleration Gate
rows.note: Locked until Slave Commander is destroyed

pockets.title: Second Pocket
pockets.prose:
Blitz: Destroy the True Sansha battlecruiser, bookmark his wreck, warp out and come back in a few minutes to pick up the loot.

Full room aggro on warp-in. The fleet is spread out in several groups at significant distances across the pocket so immediate incoming damage will be low. Most of them will be ~50 km away; one battleship will spawn at a high angle above you 90 km away and can be ignored.

True Sansha Battlecruiser will not be immediately present on warp-in. After roughly 30 seconds in the pocket a loud alarm will sound in local and (sometimes) spawn the commander. Shoot the Mind Control Tower and kill the Centus Militant Supervisor if no commander spawns to despawn the site.

rows.name: True Sansha's Phantasm/Specter
rows.cargo: Possible True Sansha faction modules

rows.name: Centus Militant Supervisor (Centus Dark Lord/Overlord)
rows.trigger: Destroying despawns site and may trigger escalation

rows.name: Centus Bunker
rows.cargo: T1 ammo

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text:
This site is very similar to Sansha Watch. 
Upon warping to the site you will land at an acceleration gate.

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.text: Destroying the True Sansha commander may escalate the site to Sansha Owned Station.

messages: Previous explorers have commented that one of the gates requires a passkey. Alternatively, it can be bypassed by convincing the commander to unlock it. The overseer guards the Mind Control Tower vigorously.

Someone has entered the vicinity of the acceleration gate, and has awakened the Slave Commander! Prepare for a fight, unless you have the means to bypass the gate's security system.
Centus Slave Commander: Fool, you've overstepped your welcome here. Minions, defend your master!

Signals coming from the Mind Control Tower resemble those used by Sansha commanders when they control their troops. The signals are emitting at a furious pace, indicating the residents of the Tower are becoming increasingly desperate.
Enemy craft have undocked from one of the Centus bunkers!

To your surprise, the Overseer seems to have spent the last moments of his life sending some message to your ship on a private channel, a fact you learn from a blinking entry on your communication panel a few seconds after his innards slid across your windshield, bounced along your fuselage and were sucked into your thrusters. It appears he wanted to save his life by telling you the whereabouts of some place you could load your cargohold with riches, but before he could get very far with his offer, his journey ended. All you have is some hysteric babble about a hidden mining station at a certain location.

Minor_Serpentis_Annex.name: Minor Serpentis Annex

pockets.title: First Pocket
pockets.prose:
----
Kill points, approach the gate, use Serpentis Crystal Tag - voilà, you are in Second Pocket. Or kill Core Militiant Commander.

pockets.title: Second Pocket
pockets.prose:
----

Notable structures on site

Shooting any of the Serpentis Towers triggers Tower wave. Shooting the Smuggler gate triggers gate wave.
If you shoot at the gate before triggering tower wave then tower wave is also triggered (verify).

Spawns can be grouped differently depending on what order they are triggered in. The following is from shooting one of the towers before shooting at the gate.

Reinforcements to tower wave arrive few seconds later.

rows.name: Shadow Serpentis Wing Leader
rows.cargo: Drops possibly Shadow Serpentis modules

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text: The site is very similar to Serpentis Watch.

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.text: Can escalate to Serpentis Owned Station

messages: Previous explorers have commented that one of the gates requires a passkey. Alternatively, it can be bypassed by convincing the commander to unlock it. The overseer guards the Smuggler Gate vigorously. There must be a way to lure out some of his guards before engaging him though ...
A distress signal is sent when the Starbase Control Tower is attacked! Hostile reinforcements are incoming!
A group of Core activists have jumped through the stargate to defend the Starbase Control Tower
Imbeciles. I'm surrounded by imbeciles! I spent a fortune on this place and you can't even defend it from some rag-tag outsiders. Pfft! I'll deal with you all after I mop the floor with these pests.
The Overseer has come to defend the stargate! Prepare for a fight.

To your surprise, the Overseer seems to have spent the last moments of his life sending some message to your ship on a private channel, a fact you learn from a blinking entry on your communication panel a few seconds after his innards slid across your windshield, bounced along your fuselage and were sucked into your thrusters. It appears he wanted to save his life by telling you the whereabouts of some place you could load your cargohold with riches, but before he could get very far with his offer, his journey ended. All you have is some hysteric babble about a hidden mining station at a certain location.

Molting_Season.name: Molting Season
intro:
This expedition escalates from Radiance.

=Walkthrough=

pockets.title: First location
pockets.prose:
Video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N6RxsLbS2Kg Gila]

Access: Gateless, Open Access 

The Sentient is the trigger for the escalation and contains loot. And is spawned from the beginning. This part can be blitzed by destroying the Sentient fast. 

Second wave is triggered by destruction of first wave.

rows.name: Sentient Domination Alvus
rows.cargo: Drone components and possibly a Sentient Sensor Booster.

pockets.title: Second location
pockets.prose: Video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIvWi3ZvwCs Gila]

rows.name: Sentient Alvus Creator
rows.cargo: Drone components.

pockets.title: Third location
pockets.prose:
During this stage you have to kill cruisers and battlecruisers. Once that's done, Sentient will spawn. If that fails, kill everything except battleships. 

Video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_nY_ABZ7Ig0 Gila]

rows.name: Sentient Alvus Creator
rows.cargo: Drops drone components.

pockets.title: Fourth location
pockets.prose:
Blitz: Shoot once (you don't even need to hit it) any of the battleships on grid and Radiant Hive Mother will spawn.

Video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s5ZBHN0BkwE Gila]

Sixth wave may be triggered by finishing off third wave.

Seventh wave may be triggered by finishing elite frigates from fifth wave.

rows.name: Radiant Hive Mother
rows.cargo: T2 salvage

messages: Among the rubble from this special station, you find a tracking device, supposedly homed in on transponders placed on units this facility has produced through the years. What the reason was for the mother hive to monitor its offspring one can only guess, but in any case it seems like this little instrument is about to spell certain doom for one of its hopefuls; one of the units seem to be still in range of this device and you get the location flashing on one of your panels.

Moving_Day.name: Moving Day
intro: Moving Day is an expedition that can escalate from Rogue Trial Yard sites.

pockets.title: First Location
pockets.prose:
----
When you warp in only the cruisers are on site. Frigates will spawn in few seconds. If you warp out before killing the first triggers the second wave will spawn on warp in.

rows.name: Sentient Viral Infector Alvum
rows.cargo: drops drone components

pockets.title: Second Location
pockets.prose:
----
Attacking anything triggers wave #2.

Attacking destroyers triggers wave 3. Subsequent spawns seem to be timed.

rows.name: Sentient Violator Alvum
rows.cargo: Drone components

rows.name: Sentient Viral Infector Alvum
rows.cargo: Sentient faction modules, drone components, 43-X Nexus Chip

blocks.title: Spawn 1, triggered by destroying commander from initial defenders

rows.name: Hive Logistic Overseer
rows.cargo: drops

messages: Mid fight you noticed a transport ship coming in from warp accompanied by a few drone escorts and after some targeted scans your instruments get a suspicious reading along their incoming warp trajectory.
In local upon clearing all drones
Drone Signal to Hive: ræsio, mission #5476 failed. Increase Security.
Not only did you find a small convoy, but mid fight, another similar convoy warped in on you. As soon as the last drones blow up, your instruments are ready with the next reading.
Not only did you find a small convoy, but mid fight, another similar convoy warped in on you. This however seems to be "it" as your scanners do not manage to sense any more incoming drone ships.

Not one, not two, but three convoys. It's starting to look like beads on a string or, rather, a trail of ants. This, however, seems to be the end of the line, as your scanners do not manage to sense any more incoming drone ships.
Not one, not two, but three convoys. This is starting to look like beads on a string or, rather, trail of ants, and there seem to be more out there!

Again you manage to get your claws into three small convoys. Killing these is easy, like stealing candy from a child. One can just follow these guys and rake up the goodies. And more are on the horizon!

All good things come to an end, this small and torn down hive was probably the old residence to those eminent machines and they busy moving everything to their new place. You kind of hope these drones don't have the capacity to bear a grudge now that you have destroyed both their old home and their future one as well. But then again, if they could, it would not matter much; you didn't leave any of them in large enough pieces to bear anything again.

Mul-Zatah_Monastery.name: Mul-Zatah Monastery
intro:
Mul-Zatah Monastery is a DED 4/10 combat site that can be scanned down with probes, and can be found in high and low security space in the Amarr regions. Alternatively it can be received as an escalation from a Blood Refuge.

The site is behind an acceleration gate. Battlecruiser hulls and below can access it. Strategic (T3) Cruisers can not enter the site.

pockets.title: Room #1
pockets.prose: Destroying all enemies unlocks the acceleration gate.

rows.name: Mul-Zatah Gatekeeper
rows.cargo: drops 7th Tier Overseer's Personal Effects and cruiser-sized faction modules

pockets.title: Room #2
pockets.prose:
No auto-aggro on warp-in. Cruiser group will primary medium and heavy drones frequently.

Destroying the Inner Sanctum structure drops 8th Tier Overseer's Personal Effects and potentially Dark Blood or Corpum C-Type modules. In rare cases, you can get an Ashimmu BPC.

rows.name: Inner Sanctum
rows.note: Doesn't DPS or EWAR, but it seems you already have enough in this pocket ¯\_(ツ)_/¯; immune to EWAR
rows.cargo: Corpum C-Type modules

rows.separator: Up group (20km away from center group)
Down group (20km away from center group)
North group (20km away from center group)
South group (20km away from center group)
West group (20km away from center group)
East group (20km away from center group)

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text:
The enemies in each room remain passive until the player takes aggressive action. Therefore, sniper-fit ships can easily and safely move to long range before starting combat, and can kill enemies well before the enemies get in range to do damage.

Short-range combat ships will face a lot of enemy cap neutralizers, so a fit that requires low or no cap to operate is recommended.

notes.title: Blitz
notes.text: Destroy all enemies in the first room, and be able to tank/avoid enough damage in the second room to destroy the Inner Sanctum. It goes down pretty quickly under fire.

rewards.title: Loot
rewards.text:
You can get about 2 million ISK in bounties and about 2 million in Overseer's Effects. Faction loot values can vary significantly.

Possible deadspace modules

messages:
The Mul-Zatah Monastic order has for a long time maintained close links with Omir Sarikusa and the Blood Raider Covenant. The order is considered by most law enforcement agents to pose a limited threat to security, since they seem to keep to themselves for the most part. They are, however, notoriously intolerant of trespassers near their monasteries and it is not advisable to approach lightly armed.
DED Threat Assessment: Risky (4 of 10)
The gates of the Mul-Zatah are fiercely guarded by a small contingency of monastic knights.

Limited information is available on the Inner Sanctum of the Mul-Zatath monasteries; and most of what is known is based on unreliable information from members of the order that have been captured in DED raids on Blood Raider strongholds. According to these cultists the Mul-Zatath engage in gruesome genetic research using Minmatar slaves legally purchased within the Amarr empire itself. The Minmatar Republic has repeatedly condemned this trade but so far with limited success.
This Mul-Zatah monastery has fallen silent at last, as have the screams of their final victims.

Nation_on_the_Rise.name: Nation on the Rise
intro:
Nation on the Rise is an expedition obtained through completion of Sansha Watch combat sites. This expedition consists of 4 different open area locations (no Acceleration gate) starting in a high security system and ending in a low security system but it can suddenly end at any step in the chain. NPC ship class encountered is Frigate, Destroyer, Cruiser, Battlecruiser and Battleship hulls. 

Warning: Elite NPC's do medium lite EWAR - Tracking Disruption, Web and Warp Scram.

pockets.title: Location 1
pockets.prose:
The initial ships will not auto-aggro on warp-in. You may have to fly some distance away from them to get within warp-in range of the Sansha ships.

Warping into the site appears to sometimes prematurely trigger the second spawn, possibly due to proximity to the Sansha Control Outpost.

Structures on site

Please note: No loot dropped from structures

rows.name: Sansha Heavy Missile Battery (Proximity Trigger 60 km)
True Sansha's Manslayer/ Enslaver
rows.cargo: Meta modules, True Sansha ammo and True Sansha tags

pockets.title: Location 2
pockets.prose:
Please note: Warping out may cause the site to disappear from your Expeditions list. Bookmark the beacon to allow you to return.

Sansha Tower Sentry III can shoot up to 250km and can deal about 200~250 dps at max range. True Sansha commander is considerably faster than the other ships and will quickly approach you.

Structures on site

rows.name: True Sansha's Manslayer
rows.cargo: Meta modules, True Sansha ammo and True Sansha tags

pockets.title: Location 3
pockets.prose:
Hint: If you are only interested in the Faction npc, he is considerably faster then the other ships. It is possible to simply tank the Sentry Towers and wait for him to get close.
Warp to site 

Message in local chat channel: 

"You have stumbled upon the enemy ship's scouting party. Prepare for a fight!"

Please note: The Tachyon Towers have a very long range and do a decent amount of dps, even with 80%+ resists.

Structures on site

pockets.title: Location (Low Security)
pockets.prose:
Warning: Your ship can be freely attacked by others - NO CONCORD INTERVENTION - in Low Security Systems (0.1 to 0.4) and Null Security Systems (0.0)

Hint: Always check Star Map statistics (Active ships, Ship kills, Pod kills, etc) of Low Security and Null Security systems first before entering. Fitting a Cloaking Device module on your ship and making more than one Safe spot will provide more safety.

The Repair Drone cruisers will periodically remote rep all hostile NPCs in this pocket for about 50-75 DPS worth while they are active.

Centus Colony General will use MWD to catch up to you if you are over 40km away, so it can be kited away from the other rats with good piloting. Speed-tanking T1 cruiser with AB and 60+ km range weapons can comfortably snipe it. It does ~100 DPS EM/Th with its turrets at ranges under 20km.

Please note: Centus Colony General has a 9,375,000.00 ISK Bounty and can drop True Sansha and Centii A-Type modules.

Structures on site (may drop loot)

rows.name: Repair Drone
rows.note: Renamed Elite Repair Drone. Does no damage

rows.name: Centus Colony General
rows.trigger: Attacking triggers 3rd Wave. Destroy to end expedition
rows.cargo: True Sansha and Centii A-Type modules

messages: All you see here are military installations and surveillance equipment, nothing that suggests this is a self sufficient base. As you warp in, a couple of ships are departing and you manage to get an approximate lock on their destination.
More ships have undocked from the Sansha Control Outpost!

This looks to be the same sort of outpost, but this time the watchers are more awake and you see a Sansha armada storm towards you. One of the ships turns away immediately though and jumps. It looks like your choices are to chase it or stay and fight.

Just before the Sansha ship blew apart, it sent out a distress call. Not that it would have helped you any, except that this call got almost an immediate reply. Your instruments have pinpointed the origins of this transmission and the resulting location glows in small, warm, orange letters on your otherwise dull looking navigation panel.
Looks like the Sansha have been constructing something huge here, probably a station ....
The Repair Drones busily repair nearby Centus ships.
The Repair Drones busily repair nearby Centus ships, but seem to have run out of power for the time being.

Centus ships have undocked from a nearby Starbase Hangar!

Centus Colony General: You dare attack my repair drones! Do you know how many slaves went into building those beauties? I'll have your head on a platter delivered straight to my Master for this barbaric attack!
Upon attacking the Centus Colony General
More Centus ships undock from a nearby Starbase Hangar to defend their leader!
Upon destroying the Centus Colony General

If the Sansha outposts you passed earlier were part of some sort of a complex with this place extended as a future centerpiece, their operation in the area seems have taken on a manner more large and ambitious than you have ever seen before.

No_Quarter.name: No Quarter
intro: No Quarter is an Expedition that can escalate from Gurista Provincial HQ.

pockets.title: Warp-in
pockets.prose: You land on an acceleration gate. Take it if no escalation is triggered from the Dread Guristas commander.

rows.name: Dread Guristas Conquistador
rows.cargo: may contain Dread Guristas faction modules or an implant

pockets.title: First pocket
pockets.prose: No enemies in the pocket. Spy drones will warp away shortly after entry.

pockets.title: Second location
pockets.prose: Destroy the Guristas Control Tower if no escalation is received from the commander battleship.

rows.name: Dread Guristas Conquistador/Destroyer
rows.cargo: may contain Dread Guristas faction modules or an implant; wreck may produce Tech 2 salvage

pockets.title: Third location
pockets.prose:
There is considerably higher damage in this pocket; the Guristas Annihilation Missile Battery does extreme EM damage and the Siege Railgun Sentries do high alpha Therm/Kin damage. Together they can destroy an improperly tanked T3C in as few as three volleys. Thus, mainly tank against EM and Kinetic damage.

Attacking the Guristas Annihilation Missile Battery triggers a defensive wave. Destroying it or the commander battleship may trigger escalation and allows you to blitz through this location.

rows.name: Dread Guristas Massacrer
rows.cargo: may contain Dread Guristas faction modules or an implant; wreck may produce T2 salvage

rows.name: Guristas Annihilation Missile Battery
rows.note: Shoots high damaging EM Cruise missiles

pockets.title: Fourth location
pockets.prose:
This location is very hard, requiring around 3-4 people in high-DPS strong tank ships. The overseer battleship has extremely strong shield reps which require the damage to exceed 1200 DPS to thermal.

Attacking the Guristas War Installation spawns two defensive waves, the second wave including the overseer.

The Siege Sentries deal a high alpha damage of 1200 mostly therm/kin per turret but fire every 16 seconds. Since there are at least 8 turrets firing at warp in, they can destroy a single T3C in two volleys if improperly tanked. It is advised to make a bookmark on-grid as you land at the site to warp to in case of danger and to reset aggro.

Terrorist Overlord Inzi Kika deals 500 DPS with turrets and nearly 1500 DPS with missiles. He has 89% EM resists, 79% Explosive and Kinetic resists, and 69% Thermal resists.

It is strongly advised to keep your ship aligned to a bouncing bookmark 200 km off, warp to it as soon as the overseer wave spawns, and snipe the spider drones, the elite frigates and then the Terrorist Overlord. His turrets reach out to 200 km and his missiles to 130 km.

rows.name: Guristas War Installation
rows.trigger: Triggers defensive waves at different damage intervals

rows.name: Terrorist Overlord Inzi Kika
rows.cargo: Wreck may contain Pith X-Type or Dread Guristas Battleship modules and may include a rare Rattlesnake BPC

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text:
The first two locations are doable solo, while the last two are much harder, with the final location requiring at least 1200 DPS minimum to break the overseer's tank. Even then it takes a long time due to the boss's strong active shield tank and high hitpoints, as well as high DPS that can tear apart a well-tanked T3 Cruiser with ease.

Warning: The DED 10/10 The Maze combat site is comparatively easy to this escalation. Use extreme caution unless you want to risk losing your ship.

messages: As the dust settles from the battle, you receive a transmission from someone claiming to be a local vigilante who congratulates you on a job well done. Your computers run a check on his ship ID's and other info they can gather on him in such a short period of time, but come up with nothing. He is at least not a part of any pirate faction, nor seems he to represent any of the official states in the galaxy. This person continues to welcome you to the area and offers to point you to some other Gurista bases he knows about and have been a menace for the local population. If you want to come and meet him, he will lead the way.

Teinei Kuma: Good to see you decided to come. I can not promise you any payment if you take on these Guristas bases, but you will earn fame among the locals and the fortune the Pirates leave behind. I'm going to send a couple of my spy drones to see if the Guristas are still where they were yesterday.
The radio crackles, it is the vigilante all excited, who whispers in a conspiratorial tone, "They are still here! Come quick and we shall introduce them to pain!

After a few exciting moments waiting for further messages, a series of less interesting moments waiting still and then a few very boring moments while your patience approaches a grand finale, you decide that this stranger must have wet himself when he saw you and used the chance to hide deep inside his Industrial.

Or maybe his 'spy drones' simply take forever and a day to accomplish their task. Either way you decide to abandon this farce and continue on with your business.
Control Tower Operator: More intruders! Maybe they're connected with the spy drones we just destroyed. I bet CONCORD sent them! Take care of 'em boys!
In local on control tower destruction
Teinei Kuma: We sure showed them! I'm actually starting to think I'll become a fighter some day. Will you teach me? Maybe after we're done ...

"We sure showed them! You're handy to have around when the missiles are flying, but there's no time to float here celebrating. We must press on! Another division of this same group happens to be close by!"

As you enter, you see your friend several hundred kilometers off target, complaining about something being rotten in the hydraulic system. With the Guristas on the other hand, it seems like all systems are go.

Teinei Kuma: I hope you will manage without me, but I am going to check the next and last target. It is one of the Guristas recruiting stations, they have these recruitment drives every now and then when they go through all major metropolitan areas in Caldari space, pick up from the sewers anything that is still breathing, gather them in places like these, give them some old rookie ships and beanie guns and let them have a go at each other! The better half of those who are still alive after a couple of months are taken in as Gurista pilots, the rest is shot, or sold to the Blood as refreshments! Anyways, they are just sitting there like ducks, we dont want them to get away, I will hold them busy till you arrive!
The Annihilation Missile Battery calls for backup from a nearby patrol!

Observatory_Flashpoint.name: Observatory Flashpoint
intro:
The Observatory Flashpoint is a combat anomaly that can be found in Pochven, intended to be run with a fleet of up to 15 ships. It is functionally unchanged from the Observatory Flashpoints found during Chapter 2 and Chapter 3 of the Triglavian Invasion. Whenever a site is completed, a new site will spawn immediately in another part of Pochven, with a hard limit of three sites in the region at a time.

The site comes pre locked, and will always be against EDENCOM.

{| style="border: 1px solid #333333; background-color:#350000; color: white;"

pockets.title: Warpin
pockets.prose: A small number of EDENCOM and Triglavian ships fighting each other on the acceleration gate. Sometimes, Sleepers may also be seen fighting at the warpin point.

pockets.title: 1st pocket
pockets.prose:
Near the warp-in, there is a large Stellar Observatory structure. On arrival, this structure is invulnerable, and guarded by one wave of EDENCOM ships. Attacking this wave will spawn a second wave of ships, and destroying enough ships from these two waves will spawn a single empire Dreadnought.

After the Revelation spawns, two additional waves of EDENCOM ships will continue to spawn. The Dreadnought will warp in roughly 40-80km from the Observatory in a random direction. Every two minutes, the Dreadnought will enter Siege for three minutes, giving itself a massive +425% damage boost, and the standard EWAR resistance of a Siege Module. The Dreadnought has a slow 12-second fire rate, but extremely high alpha damage, and a tracking speed of 10 (in line with long-range Cruiser weapons), making evasion difficult and mandating heavy tank. Additionally, the Dreadnought and each wave of EDENCOM ships can and will choose targets independently, meaning that at any given time five different fleet members may be under attack - logis beware!

The wreck of the Revelation contains a Dreadnought Systems Diagram, used to unlock the Triglavian cache at the end of the site. However, the wreck projects a large (30-50km) warp disruption field, so a fleet will either need to burn out of range of the disruption, bring a salvage ship to salvage the wreck, removing the field, or destroy the wreck by shooting it.

Once the Dreadnought is destroyed, the Stellar Observatory will become vulnerable, two more waves of EDENCOM ships will spawn, along with two Overcharge Pylons, and a friendly Liminal Zirnitra. The Zirnitra will open fire on either the EDENCOM ships or the Observatory. Flying within 5km of one of the Overcharge Pylons will give a +100% bonus to turret and launcher damage, and bringing 8 ships into range of a pylon will cause the friendly Zirnitra to enter Siege and gain +425% damage.

Destroying the Observatory triggers site completion, and spawns the main loot cache. The wreck of the Observatory projects a similar disruption field to that of the dreadnought wreck.

The site has a rough boundary with a 60km radius. Threshold Werpost sentries will attack and destroy any ship that passes these boundaries. They deal 10,000 DPS omni damage with pinpoint tracking and are completely invulnerable, serving as a boundary deterrent.

The Cache can be opened multiple times if multiple keys are brought to it.

rows.name: Empire Dreadnought
rows.cargo: Dreadnought Systems Diagram

rows.name: Stellar Observatory
rows.trigger: Killing triggers site completion and spawns Bioadaptive Schematic Cache.

rows.name: Triglavian Biocombinative Schematic Cache
rows.trigger: Destroy the Stellar Observatory to spawn
rows.note: Needs a Dreadnought Systems Diagram to open
rows.cargo: Zirnitra Blueprint Data Vault

rows.name: Threshold Werpost
rows.note: Pinpoint tracking and immune to damage. 10,000 DPS omni and targets anyone going past 60 km of the site warp-in

rewards.title: Rewards
rewards.text:
The site pays a considerable sum of ISK that varies with fleet size, ranging from around 520 million ISK per pilot for a fleet of 5, to around 230 million ISK per pilot for a fleet of 15. Including more than 15 pilots in the payout will greatly reduce total site rewards. In order to be included in the payout, pilots must be in the site, not cloaked, and either apply damage to the Observatory structure or apply remote repairs to another ship which has damaged the structure.

The loot cache can contain skillbooks for or . It can also contain a Zirnitra BPC, Supratidal Entropic Disintegrator BPC, XL Exotic Plasma Charge BPC, or capital component BPC.

Old_Meanie_-_Cultivation_Center.name: Old Meanie - Cultivation Center
intro: Old Meanie - Cultivation Center is a DED 1/10 rated combat site. It can be found by scanning cosmic signatures in high security space.

rows.name: Drifting Cask
rows.cargo: drops

rows.name: A "Lonely Heart"
rows.cargo: Metal scraps

rows.name: Biodome Gardens
rows.cargo: 1st Tier Overseer's Personal Effects, meta modules

rows.name: Stuffed Container
rows.cargo: Always contains one 2nd Tier Overseer's Effects and 0-3 Corpii C-Type modules

messages: "Old Meanie" is a mining relic. Previously it was a small mining outpost, but was raided so frequently by Serpentis pirates that it was abandoned. Today it contains some experimental biodomes, and further inside the complex Amarrians are creating a spiritual center. DED Threat Assessment: Training (1 of 10)

Amarr contracted biodomes are being built in the ruins and debris from an old mining outpost. The biodomes are vulnerable, but construction is going well. It is handled by questionable contractors, and in dealing with them, caution is advised.

The Amarr Empire claimed this deadspace area for cultural reasons. Amarrian theologists suspect the location of the complex might be important in a religious context and bluntly state that a higher power might be directly at work here. Security was outsourced to a renegade squadron of Corpus Blood Raiders. Caution is advised.

Operation_Spring_Cleaning.name: Operation Spring Cleaning
intro: Operation Spring Cleaning is an expedition that escalates from Angel Fortress and consists of 4 parts.

pockets.title: Warp-in
pockets.prose:
Loot may contain: 
High-grade Savior Epsilon Blueprint 
Domination MWD module

rows.name: Domination Nephilim/Warlord
rows.cargo: Possible Domination modules

pockets.title: First room
pockets.prose:
----
Approach either the station or the wreck for a possibility for the escalation to trigger.

pockets.title: Second Location
pockets.prose:
Ungated pocket. 

The second wave is passive until attacked or approached.

rows.name: Domination Nephilim/Saint
rows.cargo: Faction ammo/tags. Possible Domination modules or an implant; wreck can produce Tech 2 salvage

pockets.title: Third Location
pockets.prose: Again, another ungated pocket. Group 3 warps off after a short time and can be ignored.

rows.name: Domination Nephilim/Saint
rows.cargo: Faction ammo/tags. Possible Domination modules or an implant; wreck can contain Tech 2 salvage

pockets.title: Second Pocket
pockets.prose: Enemies are approximately 40 km from the warp-in point. Gist Domination Murderer has a short turret optimal of 21 km, but fires Nova cruise missiles that reach out to 120 km and deal approx. 450 points of damage. It deals Thermal and Kinetic damage with its turrets (with a slant towards thermal) and pure Explosive damage with its missiles. It also recharges shield at around 500 DPS.

rows.name: Gist Domination Murderer
rows.cargo: May contain Gist A-Type modules and possibly a Machariel BPC

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text: This escalation consists of four parts.

notes.title: First Part
notes.text: Warp in. If the Domination commander is there: kill him, possibly get escalation. Else (or If didn't get escalation): Use go to the next room to possibly get the escalation.

notes.title: Fourth and Last Location
notes.text: You land at an acceleration gate at warp-in. No enemies are present.

rewards.title: Loot
rewards.text: The Domination battleships drop faction ammo and dog tags, and may also drop Domination faction modules or even implants. The Gist Domination Murderer in the final location may drop Gist A-Type battleship modules and possibly a rare Machariel BPC.

messages: In the ruins of this Angel structure you come across some logs containing a report from a ship identified as "Angel of Death". The ship is reporting the progress of operation "Spring Cleaning", where a squadron of Angels roam around the region and wipe out anyone the they view as a threat to their domination in the area. This gang has obviously been busy the last days, the log contains long lists of "confiscated" materials, destroyed structures and recycled biomass, the last item presumably being a measure of how many people they have murdered in the process. The list is a bit vague when it comes to identifying exactly who is being killed, which target is yet to be taken out and where these places are, but you try to extract the specifics and feed it into your databanks, which then relay the info to various search engines and registers in the region in the hope of being able to pinpoint some of the locations. Soon you get feedback indicating where to find one of these places; a small research station where scientists from the Caille University have a field laboratory. Or at least had one .. if the Angels have not hit them already, there is only one way to find out.

You are obviously too late to save the scientist and students from the Angels. It looks like they might have used them for target practice. Your attention is drawn to your navigation computer, which has tried all this time to dig up another location based on the Angel logs, but to no avail.

You are obviously too late to save the scientist and students who worked here. You wonder why on earth the pirates felt threatened by this academic bunch, but then again, they may just have used them for target practice. Your attention is drawn to your navigation panel; your computers have managed to dig up another location based on the Angel logs.
This place seems to have served as a small outpost for the Angels. Not much of any importance here, and you have no idea where to go next.
This location seems to have served as a small scouting outpost for the Angels. You have co-ordinates for your next destination, but be aware that whoever is there probably knows you're coming.
Success! You managed to nail down the point of origin of these newly arrived Angels. If now only this Angel of Death guy would be there ...
A lot of individuals, fictitious as well as non fictional, have been remembered throughout history as the "Angel of Death". You very much doubt that this low down pirate will join their ranks.

Outgrowth_Rogue_Drone_Hive_(10_10).name: Outgrowth Rogue Drone Hive
intro:
Outgrowth Rogue Drone Hive is a DED 10/10 rated combat site that is found in null security space.

This site can be found by scanning cosmic signatures or as an escalation from Drone Squad, Drone Patrol, or Drone Horde.

Note that the DED 5/10 Rogue Drone site found in low is also called Outgrowth Rogue Drone Hive. See Outgrowth Rogue Drone Hive (5/10) for details on that. The two sites are very similar.

rows.name: Elite Drone Parasite
rows.cargo: Elite Drone AI

rows.name: Deserted Starbase Storage Facility
rows.cargo: 9th Overseer's Personal Effects and bunch of mineral alloys

pockets.title: Second Pocket
pockets.prose:
----

The room contains two acceleration gates. Ancient acceleration gate will take you to the third room while the surging acceleration gate will take you straight to fourth room but requires to use. It also requires Zbikoki's Hacker Card (consumed on use) found in The Right Hand of Zazzmatazz. In a fleet only one member needs to have the hacker card. Once opened the gate will stay open for 10 seconds an allow passage to everyone with the required skill without requiring new hacker card.

The Surging Acceleration Gate can be used to blitz the site by skipping the fourth and fifth pockets, but you will miss out on some of the site's loot. If you want the full loot from the site, take the Ancient Acceleration Gate.

rows.name: Elite Drone Parasite
rows.cargo: Elite Drone AI

The Kuari Strain Mother has very strong active shield repairers and large amount of hull HP. Also note that it has very long range webs that reach to 50 km.

rewards.title: Loot
rewards.text:
You will get Overseer's Personal Effects, mineral alloys and T2 salvage.

messages:
Ever since the four empires united in a coalition against Sansha's Nation all those years ago, many people have been questioning just how effective the campaign was. It is no secret that – alive or not – the remnants of Sansha Kuvakei's Nation are still quietly waging their century-old war. Not only that, but there has been rising speculation that the many advanced operations that have caught the DED's attention could only have been made possible through the auspices of someone or something more capable than disunited True Slaves.

It has become increasingly hard for the empires to ignore the frightening level of sophistication with which Sansha's twisted dystopians react to events across the cluster. This growing concern was highlighted yet again when, immediately after synth variants of the Frentix booster were legalized in empire space, Sansha strongholds deep inside Stain began production of far more potent and highly illegal versions.

Pioneers_Peril.name: Pioneers Peril
intro: Pioneers Peril is an Expedition that can escalate from Angel Military Complex. It consists of four parts or locations. The chance for it to continue to the next part is good but not guaranteed. Because of the many parts, it's advisable to use a ship that can travel well. The last part is significantly harder; consider a marauder here.

Video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eKShLk6i72o Gila (full clear)]

You land at an acceleration gate.

pockets.prose:
Videos:
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b1s5CSJCwwY Vargur],
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CXtLjL54l-o Gila]

Ungated non-deadspace pocket. No rats initially present.

Jorun 'Red Legs' Greaves deals significantly high Explosive and Kinetic damage at a fairly short range. Try to outpace her if you can. She has fairly high resists, the weakest being 66% Explosive resists, plus a strong shield tank. She has an MWD and will try to chase you at around 1700 m/s.

Attack the Space Truckers Pit Stop to spawn an optional defensive wave. This is only worth doing for extra bounties/salvage.

rows.cargo: May contain Domination or Gist A-Type modules or possibly a Machariel BPC; wreck may produce T2 Salvage

rewards.title: Loot

messages: Going through the logs from one of the command ships you blasted, you come across a recent memo containing a draft for a plan where forces from this Military Complex and another similar to this one were to gang up and raid a space trucker station somewhere in the region. Where this space trucker station is, is not included in the logs, but the location of the rally point is there. It is supposed to be by a small asteroid belt, not too far away.
From the wreckage of this ship, you get info on where it is from, it is another Angel station. Well, more an outpost than a station perhaps, but it is a pure military outfit, not a regular colony.
Again you let your scanners comb the remains of the station and the ships, looking for clues on this alleged raid, but alas ... nothing, not a word anywhere.

Again you let your scanners comb the remains of the station and the ships, looking for clues on this alleged raid, and before long you are holding a log listing the second rally spot and as far as you can see, the raiding parties have already departed from here and two other stations and are supposed to convene within the hour. If one of the raiding parties was supposed to come from the Angel station you destroyed originally, you have already managed to diminish their forces somewhat.
A fixed guidance beacon is floating here all alone. You quickly scan it but it appears the guidance system has been destroyed.

A fixed guidance beacon is floating here all alone. You quickly scan it and discover the guidance system points to a location not too far away. Perhaps thats is the space trucker station. In any case, it's the only clue you have to follow; if the pirates have ever been here, they have gone already
A peaceful station, where transport ships get refitted and refuelled. Almost too peaceful...

messages:
Pith Penal Complexes are run by the retired Amarr captain Dewak Humfry, a fiercely disciplined tactician often referred to as 'Screaming' Dewak by his prisoners. After his service in the Imperial Navy Dewak decided to go into the prison business in the private sector, and business is clearly booming.
DED Threat Assessment: Perilous (8 of 10)

This corridor is used to guard prisoners that are deemed incapable of breaking out by themself (and thus safe enough to contain in low-security facilities) but are "connected" well enough to demand a high security deadspace pocket.

Prisoners, brought here for rehabilitation, have their equipment confiscated by the authorities. Then it is "taxed" heavily to pay upkeep costs and it often leaves the prisoners without any belongings. Dewak keeps these taxes under lock and key, guarded by his number-one warden.

This site's acceleration gate allows only Frigate class ships or lower and their Tech 2 equivalents to enter the site. The "Scratched and Dented Keycard" can also be found in the Leaking Caskets in the Haunted Yard.

messages:
Supply depot for combat vessels and pirate cargo haulers alike. The Pith Guristas in these depots are very aggressive. 
 DED Threat Assessment: Minor (2 of 10)
The Pith Guristas rely on nimble fighters to stop any intruders into this complex by stationing them close to the gate-in beacon. In reality, the defenses are rather incompetent.
The Pith wheel and deal in fuel, and a lot of supplies are stored in this deadspace pocket. Aware that they could be attacked at any time, they stock up just sufficiently to meet demands.

The Pith Guristas collect and store cargo from various raids here. They liquidate their assets as fast as possible, so the actual amount being stored varies from day to day. The locales are relatively well defended.
Inside the last pocket of the Pith Merchant Depot resides the Superintendent. He oversees the collective storage space, collection of taxes and fees and manages investments. He is well guarded.

A passive shield-tanked Drake can run this site slowly. The rats are not difficult, but they are very spread out, so bring a MWD.

notes.title: Walkthrough
notes.text:
The first three locations are generally in high security space and last in low security space but this can vary. 
 
The first three locations can be done in a T1 frigate at range, though for the last location a high DPS destroyer or a cruiser is advised.

rewards.title: Loot
rewards.text: The commander drones in sites drop drone components and can also drop Rogue Drone 46-X Nexus Chip (Astero) or a faction module. The container in last location contains T2 salvage.

messages: Throughout this last fight, your radar equipment has been busy chewing on information about incoming and outgoing vessels and it seems it has traced a very large group of ships that left this place few minutes before you arrived. You have no clue why they left, were they fleeing? Or was it a coincidence? Either way, there is only one way to find out.

There is no trace of the ships themselves, but you pick up signals from a score of astrometric probes in the area. If this were not drones, one could think they were looking for a place to settle. Though faint, your instruments manage still to discern the current location of this mysterious group of ships.

There is no trace of the ships at the location, but you pick up signals from a score of astrometric probes in the area. If this were not drones, one could think they were looking for a place to settle. Sadly, all this electronic chatter seems to have confused your instruments to the point where you get no further information on the ships you were seeking.

These ships which you seem to have caught off guard, represented only a fraction of the group indicated by the signal your radars have been picking up. Moreover now the origin of the main signal seems to be close, very close.

These few ships were nowhere near many enough to be responsible for the massive signal you had picked up before and you reach the conclusion that this was probably a small contingent that split and got lost from the larger group. Sadly it seems you have lost the main fleet as well.

You don't remember having seen such a large and rabid swarm of rogue drones before, luckily they were gimpy as heck. You wonder what they were trying to defend in such a desperate manner, throwing themselves at you wave after wave until all were obliterated. The signal is weaker but still there...

When the battle is over, all is silent and you wonder why all these drones wasted themselves against your guns in such seemingly senseless manner. Not a single one left, not a single one seems to have escaped and your instruments sense nothing more out there. Even though you feel something is missing, you have no alternative but to call off the chase.

The drone transports were easy prey after you had previously wasted most of their escort ships. You wonder what they were doing here in the middle of nothing and conclude that the only plausible reason is that you must have intercepted and destroyed a new rogue drone colony in the making.

Radiance.name: Radiance
intro:
Radiance is an Unrated Complex found in nullsec via exploration. It can be blitzed as the gates aren't locked and you can trigger the boss without clearing a significant part of the site. The triggers consist of a mixture of proximity triggers and just normal NPC destruction.

Video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S26R9dGLpxg Gila]

The site is behind an acceleration gate. Warping to the site lands you at 0 on the gate.

pockets.title: First Pocket
pockets.prose: The acceleration gate in the first pocket is not locked, so you can fly to it and take the gate to the next room, and thereby skip this room altogether if you want. Be careful though, as proximity to the gate spawns additional reinforcement waves, so you need a strong tank if you chose to skip the room.

pockets.title: Second Pocket
pockets.prose:
To get the commander wave to spawn, you have to approach the Warning Sign in the corner of the station. Alternatively, it can be triggered by destroying the battlecruisers from initial defenders.
There is also a second version, where the commander wave consists of around 15 cruisers and battlecruisers instead of the battleships. 15 cruisers wave was additional one for me, which spawned battleship wave with Sentient Supreme Alvus Parasite after.
